children.text: bījaṃ śrutīnāṃ sudhanam munīnāṃ jīvañjaḍānām mahadādikānām
children.translated_text: I take refuge in a certain dark radiance, the seed of the Vedas, the excellent wealth of sages, the life of both the living and the inert, beginning with the great principle,
the fiery weapon against the sins of worldly existence.
May <s>Vighnapati</s>, whose red-limbed crest shines like a jeweled diadem, adorned with a swarm of bees greedy for the honey-water of his cheek and the honey of his frontal globes,

children.text: māṇikyamauliriva rājati yasya maulau vighnaṃ sa dhūnayatu vighnapatiḥ sadā vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: always shake away your obstacle.
May that <s>Dinakara</s>, who draws out the helpless world sinking in the middle of the deep ocean of masses of darkness,

children.text: dattvā jagattrayahitaḥ svakarāvalambaṃ vāñchāṃ sa vo dinakaraḥ saphalīkarotu ||
children.translated_text: and, beneficent to the three worlds, gives it the support of his own hand, make your wish fruitful.

May that king of <s>Kāśī</s>, who is a boat for people sinking in the ocean of disease, dreadful with crocodiles of affliction, swollen by the waters of rivers stirred up from mountains of faults caused by false eating and the like,

children.text: rogāmbudhau bhavajanasya nimajjato yaḥ potaḥ prayacchatu śubhāni sa kāśirājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: grant auspicious things.

children.text: kecitsanti nighaṇṭavo'tilaghavaḥ kecinmahāntaḥ pare kecid durgamanāmakāḥ katipaye bhāvasvabhāvojjhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Some nighaṇṭus are very small; some others are large; some have difficult names; a few are devoid of the nature of their meanings.

children.text: tasmānnātilaghurna cātivipulaḥ khyātādināmā satām prītyai dravyaguṇānvito'yamadhunā grantho mayā badhyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this book, neither too small nor too extensive, furnished with famous and other names and with the qualities of substances, is now composed by me for the delight of good people.
Everything is to be accomplished by the body; the cause of its continuance is life-span.
For whom would instruction in <s>āyurveda</s> not bring happiness?
Even there, first the names, qualities, and defects of substances are to be known.

children.text: atasta eva vakṣyante tajjñāne hi kriyākramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore those very things will be stated, for the procedure of action depends on knowledge of them.

children.text: harasya bhavane jātā haritā ca svabhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: Born in the abode of <s>Hara</s>, and green by nature,
and because it removes all diseases, it is called <s>harītakī</s>.
<s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, then <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>,
<s>Rohiṇī</s>, and <s>Cetakī</s>: <s>harītakī</s> is divided into seven kinds.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is so called from its promoting life; from its purifying it is regarded as <s>Pūtanā</s>.
It is to be known as <s>Amṛtā</s> because it is like nectar; <s>Vijayā</s> because it gives victory.
Because it gives fearlessness to people, it is celebrated as <s>Abhayā</s>.
<s>Rohiṇī</s> is so called from the increase of its virtues, and <s>Cetakī</s> from consciousness.
<s>Jīvantī</s> has the appearance of gold in color; <s>Pūtanā</s> is bony.
<s>Amṛtā</s> is said to be three-lobed; <s>Vijayā</s> has the form of a gourd.

children.text: pañcāṅgī tvabhayā jñeyā matā vṛttā tu rohiṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Abhayā</s> is to be known as five-angled, while <s>Rohiṇī</s> is considered round.
<s>Cetakī</s> is to be known as three-angled; now their action is stated.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is useful in all diseases; <s>Pūtanā</s> is beneficial in external application.
<s>Amṛtā</s> is said to be for purification; <s>Vijayā</s> removes all diseases.
<s>Abhayā</s> is praised for eye disease; <s>Rohiṇī</s> heals wounds.
<s>Cetakī</s> is for preparations of powder; thus it is declared sevenfold.
<s>Harītakī</s> is red when cut, like jaggery, somewhat sour and astringent,
thick-skinned, juicy, with little seed, and heavy.
When chewed it increases digestive fire; when ground it purifies the stool.

children.text: svinnā saṃgrāhiṇī proktā bhṛṣṭā pathyā tridoṣanut ||
children.translated_text: When boiled it is said to be binding; when roasted it is wholesome and removes the three doṣas.

children.text: grīṣme tulyaguḍāṃ susaindhavayutāṃ meghāvanaddhāmbare sārddhaṃ śarkarayā śaradyamalayā śuṇṭhyā tuṣārāgame
children.translated_text: In summer it should be joined with equal jaggery and good rock-salt; when the sky is covered by clouds, with sugar; in autumn, with <s>amalā</s>; at the coming of cold, with dry ginger;

children.text: pippalyā śiśire vasantasamaye kṣaudreṇa saṃyojitāṃ rājanprāpya harītakīmiva gadā naśyantu te śatravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in winter with long pepper, and in springtime joined with honey. O king, may your enemies perish like diseases when they have obtained <s>harītakī</s>.

children.text: śivā harītakī pathyā cetakī vijayā jayā
children.translated_text: <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Harītakī</s>, <s>Pathyā</s>, <s>Cetakī</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>,
<s>Prapathyā</s>, <s>Pramathā</s>, <s>Amoghā</s>, <s>Kāyasthā</s>, <s>Prāṇadā</s>, and <s>Amṛtā</s>;
<s>Jīvanīyā</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Pṛtanā</s>, and <s>Abhayā</s>,

children.text: vayasthā nandinī jñeyā śreyasī rohiṇī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vayasthā</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Śreyasī</s>, and also <s>Rohiṇī</s> are to be known.
<s>Harītakī</s> has five tastes, lacking salt, with a predominance of astringency.
It is dry, hot, kindles digestion, promotes intellect, has a sweet post-digestive taste, and is rejuvenative.
It is laxative, gives intelligence and long life, benefits the eyes, is nourishing, and is light.
It draws away asthma, cough, urinary disorders, piles, skin disease, swelling, abdominal disease, worms,
hoarseness, disorder of the bowels, constipation, irregular fever,
abdominal tumors, distension, wounds, vomiting, hiccup, itching, and heart disease,
jaundice, colic, abdominal obstruction, and spleen disease.
By its sweet and sour nature <s>harītakī</s> destroys vāta; by its astringent and sweet nature,
it destroys pitta, and likewise kapha by its pungency.
One exhausted by travel, deficient in vigor, dry, emaciated, and wasted by fasting,

children.text: pittādhiko garbhavatī ca nārī jvaryalpavīryastvabhayāṃ na khādet ||
children.translated_text: as well as a woman with excess pitta, a pregnant woman, one with fever, or one of little strength, should not eat <s>Abhayā</s>.
<s>Dhātrīphala</s>, <s>Amṛtaphala</s>, <s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Śrīphala</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>:
likewise <s>dhātrīphala</s> is aphrodisiac and especially conquers bleeding disorders.
Because of its sourness it destroys wind; because of sweetness and coolness, pitta;

children.text: kaphaṃ rūkṣakaṣāyatvāt tasmāt kim adhikam phalam ||
children.translated_text: because of dryness and astringency, kapha. Therefore what fruit is superior?
Because of its sourness, should it not produce pitta; because of sweetness and coolness, kapha;

children.text: vātaṃ rūkṣakaṣāyatvād evaṃ kiṃ na viparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because of dryness and astringency, vāta? Thus why would the reverse not occur?
The fact that <s>dhātrī</s> destroys the three doṣas is remembered by the sages as due to its power alone.
The causality of taste and the rest has also been stated because of plausibility.
<s>Vibhītaka</s>, <s>Karṣaphala</s>, <s>Bhūtāvāsa</s>, <s>Kalidruma</s>,
<s>Vāsanta</s>, <s>Akṣa</s>, born in the <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, and <s>Tilapuṣpaka</s>;
<s>Vibhītaka</s> has a sweet post-digestive taste, is astringent, and removes kapha and pitta.
It is hot in potency, cool to the touch, purgative, and destroys cough.
It is dry, beneficial for the eyes, good for the hair; from its kernel comes an intoxicating effect.
With these three fruits, <s>Triphalā</s> arises, excellent, the best of fruits.
<s>Triphalā</s> destroys skin disease, urinary disorder, blood disorder, kapha, and pitta.

children.text: cakṣuṣyā ropaṇī hṛdyā vayasaḥ sthāpanī sarā ||
children.translated_text: It benefits the eyes, heals, is good for the heart, stabilizes age, and is laxative.
<s>Bhūdhātrī</s>, having many leaves, is <s>Jaṭātāmalakī</s> and <s>Śivā</s>.
<s>Bhūdhātrī</s> aggravates <s>vāta</s>; it is bitter, astringent, sweet, and cooling.
It removes thirst, cough, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, <s>kapha</s>, pallor, and wounds.
The earlier <s>āmalaka</s> is called <s>prācī</s>, while <s>nāgara</s> is considered the red variety.
When ripe it produces <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>; when dry it is heavy and conquers wind.
<s>Vāsā</s> is called <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>siṃhamukhā</s>, physician's-mother, and <s>aṭarūṣaka</s>.

children.text: śuklā haimavatī caiva siṃhī syād vājidantikā
children.translated_text: It is also <s>śuklā</s>, <s>haimavatī</s>, <s>siṃhī</s>, and <s>vājidantikā</s>.
<s>Vāsaka</s> aggravates <s>vāta</s>, is good for the voice, and destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood disorders.
It removes asthma, cough, fever, vomiting, urinary disease, skin disease, and wasting.
<s>Guḍūcī</s> is called <s>kuṇḍalī</s>, <s>chinnā</s>, <s>vayasthā</s>, and <s>amṛtavallarī</s>.
It is <s>chinnodbhavā</s>, <s>chinnaruhā</s>, <s>amṛtakandā</s>, and <s>vilāsinī</s>.
It is <s>vatsādanī</s>, <s>candrahāsā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, and <s>cakralakṣaṇā</s>.
<s>Guḍūcī</s> is pungent, light, sweet in digestion, and rejuvenative.
It is absorbent, astringent, hot, aphrodisiac, bitter, and kindles the digestive fire.
It overcomes jaundice, skin disease, gouty blood disorders, fever, <s>pitta</s>, and worms.

children.text: ghṛtena vātaṃ saguḍā vibandham pittaṃ sitāḍhyā madhunā kaphaṃ ca
children.translated_text: With ghee it pacifies <s>vāta</s>; with jaggery, constipation; with sugar, <s>pitta</s>; and with honey, <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: vātāsram ugraṃ rubutailamiśrā śuṃṭhyāmavātaṃ śamayed guḍūcī ||
children.translated_text: Mixed with the oil named in the text it pacifies severe gouty disorder, and with dry ginger it pacifies <s>āmavāta</s>.
<s>Bilva</s> is called <s>śalāṭu</s>, <s>śailūṣa</s>, <s>mālūra</s>, and <s>sadāphala</s>.
It is considered <s>lakṣmīphala</s>, <s>gandhagarbha</s>, <s>śāṇḍilya</s>, and thorny.
<s>Bilva</s> is constipating, astringent, hot, pungent, kindling, and digestive.

children.text: hṛdyam bālaṃ laghu snigdhaṃ tiktaṃ vātakaphāpaham ||
children.translated_text: When young it is heart-beneficial, light, unctuous, bitter, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
When old it is heavy, involves all three <s>doṣas</s>, hard to digest, and has foul wind.
It causes burning and obstruction, is sweet, and weakens the digestive fire.
The pulp of <s>bilva</s> removes <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, <s>āma</s>, and colic.
<s>Agnimantha</s> is called <s>jaya</s>, <s>ketu</s>, <s>araṇi</s>, and <s>vaijayantikā</s>.
<s>Agnimantha</s> removes swelling; its potency is hot, and it reduces <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Pāṭalā</s> is called <s>kāmadūtī</s>, <s>kumbhīkā</s>, and <s>kālavṛntikā</s>.
It is <s>sthālyamoghā</s>, <s>madhodūrtī</s>, <s>tāmrapuṣpā</s>, and <s>ambuvāsinī</s>.
Another, white variety growing from the fruit is <s>kumbhīkā</s>, the woody <s>pāṭalā</s>.
<s>Pāṭalā</s> destroys anorexia, swelling, piles, asthma, thirst, and vomiting.
Its flower is not hot, astringent, and sweet, and it reduces <s>kapha</s> and blood disorders.
The fruit removes bilious diarrhea and burning, and conquers hiccup, bleeding, and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Kāśmīrī</s> is <s>sarvatobhadrā</s>, <s>śrīparṇī</s>, and <s>kṛṣṇavṛntikā</s>.
<s>Gambhārī</s>, <s>kāśmarī</s>, <s>hīrā</s>, and <s>bhadraparṇikā</s> are names of <s>kāśmaryā</s>.
<s>Kāśmarī</s> removes fever and pain; its potency is hot, and it is sweet and heavy.
Its flower is wind-producing, constipating, and removes <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, and female discharge.

children.text: phalaṃ rasāyanaṃ keśyaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ śukralaṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: The fruit is rejuvenative, good for the hair, nourishing, semen-promoting, and heavy.
It removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, wasting, thirst, blood disorders, urinary trouble, and constipation.
<s>Śyonāka</s> is <s>pṛthuśimba</s>, <s>śukanāsa</s>, and <s>kuṭannaṭa</s>.
It is <s>bhūtavṛkṣa</s>, <s>ṭuṇṭuka</s> with hard bark, <s>śalaka</s>, and <s>aralu</s>.
It is <s>mayūrajaṅgha</s>, <s>bhallūka</s>, and <s>priyañjīva</s>.

children.text: kaṭambharaḥ śyonāko dīpanaḥ pāke kaṭus tuvarako himaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭambhara</s>, namely <s>śyonāka</s>, is digestive; in digestion it is pungent, slightly astringent, and cooling.
It is absorbent, bitter, and destroys <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, cough, and <s>āma</s>.
With these five beginning with <s>bilva</s>, there is the great <s>pañcamūla</s>, which strongly kindles fire.
It is light, hot, bitter and astringent in taste, and removes fat, <s>kapha</s>, asthma, and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Gokṣura</s> is <s>trikaṭa</s>, <s>kaṇṭaphala</s>, and <s>svādukaṇṭaka</s>.
It is <s>gokaṇṭaka</s>, edible-thorn, <s>trikaṇṭa</s>, and <s>vyāladaṃṣṭraka</s>.
It is <s>śvadaṃṣṭra</s>, <s>sthalaśṛṅgāṭa</s>, <s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>, and <s>kṣurakastrika</s>.
<s>Gokṣura</s> is cooling and sweet, gives strength, and purifies the bladder.
It conquers diabetes and urinary disorders, asthma, cough, stones, dysuria, heart disease, and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: śāliparṇī dhruvā saumyā triparṇī pītanī sthirā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śāliparṇī</s> is <s>dhruvā</s>, <s>saumyā</s>, <s>triparṇī</s>, <s>pītanī</s>, and <s>sthirā</s>.
It is also <s>vidārigandhā</s>, <s>atiguhā</s>, <s>dīrghamūlā</s>, and <s>aṃśumatī</s>.
<s>Śāliparṇī</s> is heavy and removes vomiting, fever, asthma, and diarrhea.
It removes wasting and the three <s>doṣas</s>; it is nourishing, hot, and rejuvenative.
<s>Pṛṣṭhiparṇī</s> is <s>kroṣṭupucchī</s>, <s>dhāvanī</s>, <s>kalaśī</s>, and <s>guhā</s>.
It is <s>śṛgālavṛntā</s>, <s>aṅghribalā</s>, <s>pṛthakparṇī</s>, and <s>parṇikā</s>.
<s>Pṛśniparṇī</s> is light, aphrodisiac, sweet, and hot, and it destroys
bloody diarrhea, thirst, burning, the three <s>doṣas</s>, vomiting, and fever.
<s>Bṛhatī</s> is <s>sthūlabhaṇṭākī</s>, <s>viśadā</s>, and <s>mahoṭikā</s>.

children.text: vārtākī mahatī siṃhī kaṇṭakī rāṣṭrikā kulī ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>vārtākī</s>, <s>mahatī</s>, <s>siṃhī</s>, <s>kaṇṭakī</s>, <s>rāṣṭrikā</s>, and <s>kulī</s>.
<s>Bṛhatī</s> is constipating, heart-beneficial, digestive, and conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It is hot and removes skin disease, fever, asthma, colic, cough, and weak digestion.
<s>Kaṇṭālikā</s>, <s>kaṇṭakinī</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, and <s>nidagdhikā</s>,

children.text: duḥsparśā dhāvanī kṣudrā syād vyāghrī duḥpradharṣiṇī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Duḥsparśā</s>, <s>dhāvanī</s>, <s>kṣudrā</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, and <s>duḥpradharṣiṇī</s> are its names.
The white small variety is <s>candrahāsā</s>, <s>lakṣmaṇā</s>, and <s>kṣetradūtikā</s>.

children.text: kaṇṭakārī sarā tiktā kaṭukā dīpanī laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇṭakārī</s> is fluid-promoting, bitter, pungent, digestive, and light.
It is dry, hot, and digestive, and it destroys cough, asthma, fever, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys coryza, pain in the side, dysuria, and heart disorders.
The white small variety is described likewise, but especially as promoting conception.
The short <s>pañcamūla</s> is made from the five beginning with <s>gokṣura</s>.
It is strengthening, removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>, is not excessively hot, sweet, and nourishing.
From these two groups of five roots, <s>daśamūla</s> is declared.
It conquers the three <s>doṣas</s>, asthma, cough, headache, and tetanic disorders,
as well as drowsiness, sweating, fever, abdominal distension, anorexia, and pain in the side.

children.text: ṛddhiḥ sukhaṃ yugaṃ lakṣmīḥ siddhiḥ sarvajanapriyā
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> is called <s>sukha</s>, <s>yuga</s>, <s>lakṣmī</s>, <s>siddhi</s>, and <s>sarvajanapriyā</s>.

children.text: ṛṣiśreṣṭhā rathāṅgī syān maṅgalā śrāvaṇī vasuḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>ṛṣiśreṣṭhā</s>, <s>rathāṅgī</s>, <s>maṅgalā</s>, <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, and <s>vasu</s>.
<s>Yogya</s>, <s>yugyā</s>, <s>tuṣṭi</s>, <s>rāśi</s>, and <s>vṛddhi</s> are also names for it.

children.text: ṛddhir balyā tridoṣaghnī śukralā madhurā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> is strengthening, destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, promotes semen, and is sweet and heavy.
It promotes growth, bestows conception, is cooling and aphrodisiac, and removes cough, wasting disease, and ailments.
<s>Kākolī</s> is sweet; it is also called <s>Vīrā</s>, <s>Kāyasthā</s>, and <s>Kṣīraśuklikā</s>.
It may be called <s>Dhvāṃkṣolī</s>, <s>Vāyasolī</s>, <s>Svādumāṃsī</s>, and <s>Payasvinī</s>.
The second, <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, is known as <s>Śatāhvā</s> and <s>Kṣīriṇī</s>.
The pair of <s>Kākolī</s> plants is cooling, semen-promoting, sweet, and heavy.
It overcomes wind, burning, blood disorders, pitta, wasting, thirst, and fevers.
<s>Medā</s> should be known as <s>Śāliparṇī</s>, <s>Divyā</s>, <s>Medobhavā</s>, and <s>Adhvarā</s>.
<s>Mahāmedā</s> is <s>Vasucchidrā</s>, <s>Nṛdantī</s>, and <s>Devatāmaṇi</s>.
The pair of <s>Medā</s> plants is heavy, sweet, aphrodisiac, and productive of breast milk and kapha.
It is nourishing and cooling, and removes pitta, blood disorders, wasting, and wind.
<s>Jīvaka</s> is sweet; it is called <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Hrasvāṅga</s>, and <s>Kūrcaśīrṣaka</s>.

children.text: ṛṣabho dhīra indrākṣo viṣāṇī durdharo vṛṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣabha</s> is <s>Dhīra</s>, <s>Indrākṣa</s>, <s>Viṣāṇī</s>, <s>Durdhara</s>, and <s>Vṛṣa</s>.
<s>Jīvaka</s> and <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s> give strength, are cooling, and produce semen and kapha.
They remove pitta, burning, blood disorders, emaciation, wind, wasting, and diseases.
The <s>Aṣṭavarga</s>, made up of these eight substances, is cooling and very semen-promoting.
It is nourishing, destroys pitta, burning, blood disorders, and wasting, and promotes breast milk and pregnancy.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is <s>Jīvanī</s>, <s>Jīvā</s>, <s>Jīvanīyā</s>, and <s>Yaśaskarī</s>.
It is <s>Śākaśreṣṭhā</s>, <s>Jīvabhadrā</s>, <s>Maṅgalyā</s>, and <s>Jīvavardhinī</s>.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is cooling, sweet, unctuous, and removes the three doṣas.
It is rejuvenating, strength-giving, beneficial to the eyes, absorbent, and light.
<s>Madhuyaṣṭī</s> is <s>Klītanaka</s>, <s>Yaṣṭīmadhu</s>, and <s>Madhūlikā</s>.
It is called <s>Yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Yaṣṭīmadhuka</s>, <s>Jalajā</s>, and <s>Madhu</s>.
<s>Madhuyaṣṭī</s> is heavy, cooling, strengthening, and removes thirst, vomiting, and pitta.
<s>Māṣaparṇī</s> is <s>Kṛṣṇavṛntā</s>, <s>Kāmbojī</s>, and <s>Hayapucchikā</s>.
It is <s>Māṃsamāṣā</s>, <s>Siṃhamukhī</s>, <s>Svādumāṣā</s>, and <s>Mahāsahā</s>.
<s>Mudgaparṇī</s> is <s>Kṣudrasahā</s>, <s>Śūrpaparṇī</s>, and <s>Kuraṅginī</s>.
It is <s>Vanajā</s>, <s>Riṅgaṇī</s>, <s>Śivī</s>, <s>Siṃhī</s>, and <s>Mārjāragandhikā</s>.
<s>Māṣaparṇī</s> is cooling, bitter, dry, and productive of semen and strength.
It is sweet and absorbent, and removes wasting, wind, pitta, fever, and blood disorders.
<s>Mudgaparṇī</s> is the same; it removes the three doṣas and blood disorders, and is light.
<s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Śūrpaparṇī</s>, the two <s>Kākolī</s>s, <s>Jīvaka</s>, and <s>Ṛṣabha</s>,
together with <s>Medā</s> and <s>Yaṣṭī</s>, are remembered as the sweet, life-promoting group.
It produces semen, is nourishing and cooling, and gives breast milk, pregnancy, and kapha.
It removes raktapitta, thirst, wasting, fever, burning, and wounds.
<s>Eraṇḍa</s> is called <s>Dīrghadaṇḍa</s>, <s>Taruṇa</s>, and <s>Vardhamānaka</s>.
It is <s>Citra</s>, <s>Pañcāṅgula</s>, <s>Vyāghrapuccha</s>, and <s>Gandharvahastaka</s>.
Red <s>Eraṇḍa</s> is <s>Hastikarṇa</s>, <s>Vyāghra</s>, and <s>Vyāghrataloruvu</s>.
It is <s>Uttānapattra</s>, <s>Durvāta</s>, <s>Āmavairī</s>, and <s>Cañcula</s>.
The two kinds of <s>Eraṇḍa</s> are sweet, hot, and heavy, and they destroy
swelling, pain in the waist, bladder, and head, abdominal disease, and fever.
They also destroy bradhna, asthma, kapha, abdominal distension, cough, skin disease, āma, and wind.
Its fruit is purgative, sweet, strong in essence, hot, and conquers wind.
<s>Sārivā</s> is <s>Śāradā</s>, <s>Sphoṭā</s>, <s>Gopakanyā</s>, and <s>Pratānikā</s>.
It is <s>Gopāṅganā</s>, <s>Gopavallī</s>, <s>Latāhvā</s>, and <s>Kāṣṭhasārivā</s>.
Another <s>Sārivā</s> is <s>Kṛṣṇamūlī</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, and <s>Candanasārivā</s>.
The pair of <s>Sārivā</s> plants is sweet, unctuous, semen-producing, and heavy.
It destroys the three doṣas, blood disorders, vaginal discharge, fever, and diarrhea.
<s>Yāsa</s> is <s>Marudbhava</s>, <s>Anantā</s>, <s>Dīrghamūla</s>, and <s>Yavāsaka</s>.
It is <s>Bālapattra</s>, <s>Samudrānta</s>, <s>Dūramūla</s>, and <s>Atikaṇṭaka</s>.
<s>Dhanvayāsa</s> is <s>Tāmramūlī</s>, <s>Duḥsparśā</s>, and <s>Durālabhā</s>.
It is <s>Vāsaka</s>, <s>Kacchurā</s>, <s>Tāmramūlā</s>, and <s>Dhanvayavāsaka</s>.

children.text: yāsaḥ svāduḥ sarastikto himaḥ pittaharo laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yāsa</s> is sweet, juicy and bitter, cooling, pitta-removing, and light.
It destroys blood disorders, kapha, and dizziness; <s>Dhanvayavāsaka</s> is the same.

children.text: muṇḍī bhikṣuḥ parivrājī śrāvaṇī syāt tapodhanā
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍī</s> is <s>Bhikṣu</s>, <s>Parivrājī</s>, <s>Śrāvaṇī</s>, and <s>Tapodhanā</s>.
It is <s>Śrāvaṇā</s>, <s>Śrīmatī</s>, <s>Muṇḍā</s>, bitter <s>Śravaṇaśīrṣakā</s>.

children.text: muṇḍī tiktā kaṭuḥ pāke vīryoṣṇā madhurā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍī</s> is bitter, pungent in digestion, hot in potency, sweet, and light.
It benefits the intellect and conquers scrofula, vomiting, worms, disorders of the womb, pain, and anemia.
<s>Mahāmuṇḍī</s> is regarded as <s>Lobhanīyā</s> and <s>Chinnagranthinikā</s>.
It is <s>Bhūtavṛkṣā</s>, <s>Kulahalā</s>, <s>Alambuṣā</s>, and <s>Bhūkadambikā</s>.
<s>Kadambapuṣpī</s>, or <s>Bhūmikadambaka</s>, is like <s>Muṇḍī</s> in its properties.
<s>Apāmārga</s> is <s>Śikharī</s>, <s>Kiṇihī</s>, and <s>Kharamañjarī</s>.
It is <s>Adhaḥśalya</s>, <s>Śaikharika</s>, <s>Pratyakpuṣpī</s>, and <s>Mayūraka</s>.
<s>Apāmārga</s> is juicy, sharp, kindles digestion, and removes kapha and wind.
It destroys ringworm, sidhma skin disease, hemorrhoids, itching, colic, abdominal disease, and scrofula.
Another red variety, with round fruit, is <s>Vaśira</s> and <s>Kapipippalī</s>.
The reddish <s>Apāmārga</s> obstructs wind and feces and destroys kapha.
It is deficient in the former properties and dry; its leaf conquers raktapitta.
<s>Kampilla</s> is <s>Rocana</s>, <s>Raktacūrṇaka</s>, and wound-cleansing.
It is considered <s>Lohita</s>, blood-pacifying, purgative, and <s>Rañjanaka</s>.
<s>Kampilla</s> destroys kapha, pitta, blood disorders, worms, gulma, abdominal disease, and wounds.

children.text: hanti recī kaṭūṣṇaśca tacchākaṃ grāhi śītalam ||
children.translated_text: It is purgative, pungent and hot; its leafy vegetable is absorbent and cooling.
<s>Dantī</s> is <s>Ghuṇapriyā</s>, <s>Nāgadantī</s>, and <s>Śīghrānukūlinī</s>.
It is <s>Upacitrā</s>, <s>Nikumbhā</s>, <s>Viśalyā</s>, and <s>Udumbaracchadā</s>.
It is <s>Ākhuparṇī</s>, <s>Viṣairaṇḍā</s>, <s>Dravantī</s>, and <s>Śambarī</s>.
It is called <s>Mūsikāhvā</s>, <s>Sutaśreṇī</s>, <s>Pratyakśreṇī</s>, and <s>Phañjikā</s>.
The two kinds of <s>Dantī</s> are mobile, pungent in digestion and taste, and digestive-kindling.
They are sharp and hot, and destroy pitta, blood disorders, kapha, swelling, abdominal disease, and worms.
<s>Jayapāla</s>, known as <s>Dantibīja</s>, has the fruit called <s>Tittirīphala</s>.
<s>Jayapāla</s> is heavy, unctuous, purgative, and removes pitta and kapha.
<s>Mūrvā</s>, <s>Madhurasā</s>, <s>Devī</s>, <s>Pṛthakparṇī</s>, and also <s>Triparṇī</s>;
<s>Devaśreṇī</s>, <s>Svādurasā</s>, <s>Snigdhaparṇī</s>, and <s>Moraṭā</s>;
<s>Jālinī</s>, <s>Dīpanī</s>, <s>Tiktavalkalā</s>, and <s>Pṛthaktvacā</s>;

children.text: madhuśravā madhuśreṇī sruvā madhumatī ca sā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Madhuśravā</s>, <s>Madhuśreṇī</s>, <s>Sruvā</s>, and <s>Madhumatī</s>: it is that plant.

children.text: laghuparṇī madhūlī ca pīluparṇī ca pīlunī
children.translated_text: <s>Laghuparṇī</s>, <s>Madhūlī</s>, <s>Pīluparṇī</s>, and <s>Pīlunī</s>;

children.text: gopavallī tejanī ca mūrvā vṛṣyā balapradā
children.translated_text: <s>Gopavallī</s> and <s>Tejanī</s>. <s>Mūrvā</s> is aphrodisiac and gives strength;
it produces phlegm, removes pitta and vāta, is absorbent, and destroys abdominal tumors.
<s>Tṛvṛt</s>, <s>Kumbhāruṇā</s>, <s>Tryasrā</s>, <s>Bhaṇḍī</s>, and <s>Koṭaravāsinī</s>;
<s>Sarvānubhūti</s>, <s>Trivṛtā</s>, <s>Tripuṭā</s>, <s>Saralā</s>, and <s>Sitā</s>.

children.text: tṛvṛt tiktā sarā rūkṣā svādur uṣṇā samīranut
children.translated_text: <s>Tṛvṛt</s> is bitter, flowing, dry, sweet, hot, and removes vāta;
it is pungent in post-digestive taste and removes fever, phlegm, pitta, swelling, and abdominal disease.
Black <s>tṛvṛt</s> is <s>Kālameṣī</s>, <s>Kālaparṇī</s>, and <s>Ardhacandrikā</s>;
it is <s>Suṣeṇā</s>, <s>Mālavikā</s>, and is considered <s>Masūravidalā</s>.
Black <s>tṛvṛt</s> is inferior in qualities; its purgative action is sharp,
causing fainting, burning, intoxication, dizziness, and irritation of the throat.
<s>Aindravāruṇī</s>, and likewise <s>Indrāhvā</s>, <s>Vṛṣabhākṣī</s>, and <s>Gavādinī</s>;
<s>Indravāru</s>, <s>Kṣudraphalā</s>, <s>Viśālā</s>, <s>Aindrī</s>, and <s>Vṛṣādinī</s>.
Another <s>indravāruṇī</s> is <s>Citraphalā</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, and <s>Mahāphalā</s>;
<s>Ātmarakṣā</s>, <s>Nāgadantī</s>, <s>Trapusī</s>, and <s>Gajacirbhaṭī</s>;
<s>Śvetapuṣpā</s>, <s>Mṛgākṣī</s>, and likewise it is considered <s>Yakṣasurā</s>;

children.text: marudbhavā kṛmīkumbhā citrā devī ca kīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Marudbhavā</s>, <s>Kṛmīkumbhā</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, and <s>Devī</s> are also named.

children.text: indravārudvayaṃ tiktaṃ kaṭu pāke saraṃ laghu
children.translated_text: The two kinds of <s>Indravāru</s> are bitter, pungent in post-digestive taste, flowing, and light;
hot in potency, they remove jaundice, pitta, kapha, spleen disease, and abdominal disease.
<s>Āragvadha</s>, <s>Rājavṛkṣa</s>, <s>Śamyāka</s>, and <s>Kṛtamālaka</s>;
<s>Vyādhighāta</s>, <s>Karṇikāra</s>, <s>Pragraha</s>, and <s>Caturaṅgula</s>;
<s>Ārogyaśimbī</s>, <s>Svarṇadru</s>, <s>Karṇī</s>, and it is considered <s>Dīrghaphala</s>.
<s>Āragvadha</s> is heavy, sweet, cold, and a mild purgative;
it conquers fever, heart disease, pitta, blood disorders, vāta, upward movement of vāta, and colic.
Its flower increases vāta, is absorbent and bitter, and removes pitta and kapha;
its pith is sweet in post-digestive taste, unctuous, and conquers pitta and vāta.
<s>Nīlinī</s>, <s>Nīlikā</s>, <s>Grāmyā</s>, <s>Śrīphalā</s>, and <s>Bhāravāhinī</s>;

children.text: rañjinī kālikā melā tūṇī tutthā viśodhinī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rañjinī</s>, <s>Kālikā</s>, <s>Melā</s>, <s>Tūṇī</s>, <s>Tutthā</s>, and <s>Viśodhinī</s>.
<s>Nālinī</s> is purgative, bitter, beneficial for hair, and brings delusion and dizziness;
being hot, it destroys abdominal disease, spleen disease, gouty blood disorder, kapha, and vāta.
<s>Kaṭukā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Tiktā</s>, <s>Cakrāṅgā</s>, and <s>Kaṭurohiṇī</s>;
<s>Matsyapittā</s>, <s>Kāṇḍaruhā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇabhedā</s>, and <s>Dvijāṅgikā</s>;
<s>Aśokarohiṇī</s>, <s>Matsyaśakalā</s>, and <s>Śakulādinī</s>.

children.text: kaṭukī kaṭukā pāke tiktā rūkṣā sarā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭukī</s> is pungent and bitter in post-digestive taste, dry, flowing, and light;
cold, it destroys worms, asthma, burning, pitta, kapha, and fever.
<s>Aṅkollaka</s>, <s>Tāmraphala</s>, <s>Pītasāra</s>, and <s>Nikocaka</s>;
<s>Guptasneha</s>, it is purgative, and also <s>Bhūsutā</s> and <s>Dīrghakīlaka</s>.
<s>Aṅkollaka</s> is pungent, unctuous, sharp, hot, astringent, and light;
it is purgative and removes worms, colic, āma, wasting, phlegm, and poison.

children.text: tatphalaṃ śītalaṃ svādu śleṣmalam bṛṃhaṇaṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: Its fruit is cold, sweet, phlegm-producing, nourishing, and heavy;
it strengthens, is purgative, and conquers vāta, pitta, burning, wasting, and blood disorders.
<s>Sehuṇḍa</s> is <s>Vajratuṇḍa</s>, <s>Gaṇḍīra</s>, and <s>Vajradaṇḍaka</s>;
<s>Snuhī</s>, <s>Samantadugdhā</s>, <s>Asipatra</s>, <s>Vajrī</s>, and <s>Mahātaru</s>.

children.text: sehuṇḍo recanas tīkṣṇo dīpanaḥ kaṭuko guruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sehuṇḍa</s> is purgative, sharp, digestive, pungent, and heavy;
it destroys colic, āma, abdominal lumps, distension, abdominal tumors, swelling, abdominal disease, and vāta,
as well as latent poison, spleen disease, skin disease, insanity, stone, and pallor.
<s>Nimba</s>, <s>Niyamana</s>, <s>Netā</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, and <s>Pāribhadraka</s>;
<s>Sutikta</s>, <s>Sarvatobhadra</s>, <s>Picumanda</s>, and <s>Subhadraka</s>.
<s>Nimba</s> is cold, light, absorbent, pungent in post-digestive taste, and increases digestive fire and vāta;
it removes wounds, pitta, kapha, vomiting, skin disease, nausea, and urinary disorders.
The leaf of <s>nimba</s> is remembered as good for the eyes and as removing worms, pitta, and poison;
it increases vāta, is pungent in post-digestive taste, and removes every loss of appetite and skin disease.
Unripe <s>nimba</s> ripens what is immature, and the ripe one purifies;
its fruit is splitting, unctuous, hot, skin-disease-removing, and light.
<s>Mahānimba</s>, <s>Nimbavara</s>, <s>Kārmuka</s>, and <s>Viṣamuṣṭika</s>;
<s>Ramyaka</s>, <s>Girikodreka</s>, <s>Kṣīra</s>, and <s>Keśamuṣṭika</s>.
<s>Kaivarta</s>, <s>Śākaśāla</s>, <s>Giripatra</s>, and <s>Supārśvaka</s>.

children.text: mahānimbo himo rūkṣas tikto grāhī kaṣāyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahānimba</s> is cold, dry, bitter, absorbent, and astringent in post-digestive taste;
it conquers kapha, pitta, worms, vomiting, skin disease, nausea, and blood disorders.
<s>Kirātatikta</s>, <s>Kairāta</s>, <s>Bhūnimba</s>, and <s>Rāmasenaka</s>;
<s>Kirātatiktaka</s>, <s>Haima</s>, <s>Kāṇḍatikta</s>, and <s>Kirātaka</s>.
Another variety is called <s>Naipāla</s>, which ends fever.
<s>Nāḍītikta</s>, <s>Ardhatikta</s>, <s>Nidrāri</s>, and <s>Sannipātahā</s>;

children.text: kirāto vātalo rūkṣaḥ śītas tiktako laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kirāta</s> increases vāta, is dry, cold, bitter, and light;
it removes sannipāta fever, asthma, kapha, pitta, blood disorders, and burning.
It is flowing, light, bitter, and cold, and destroys balāsa, pitta, blood disorders, swelling, fever, cough, and thirst.
<s>Bhūnimba</s> increases vāta, is dry, and removes kapha, pitta, and fever.
<s>Kuṭaja</s>, <s>Kūṭaja</s>, <s>Koṭī</s>, <s>Vatsaka</s>, and <s>Girimallikā</s>;
<s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Mallikāpuṣpa</s>, <s>Indravṛkṣa</s>, and then <s>Vṛkṣaka</s>;
<s>Tucchaka</s>, <s>Varatikta</s>, <s>Śakradru</s>, and <s>Pāṇḍuradruma</s>;
<s>Śatakratudruma</s>, <s>Kośī</s>, <s>Nīlayaṣṭi</s>, and <s>Mallikā</s>.

children.text: kuṭajaḥ kaṭuko rūkṣo dīpanas tuvaro himaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṭaja</s> is pungent, dry, digestive, astringent, and cold;
it removes piles, diarrhea, pitta, blood disorders, kapha, thirst, āma, and skin disease.
Its fruits are <s>Indrayava</s>, <s>Śakrāhva</s>, and <s>Kaliṅgaka</s>;
and its seeds, called <s>Vatsakabīja</s>, are also known as <s>Bhadrayava</s>.
<s>Indrayava</s> destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, is binding, cooling, and pungent.
It removes fever, diarrhea, bleeding piles, worms, skin disease, and erysipelas.

children.text: madanaś chardano rāṭhaḥ piṇḍī piṇḍītakaḥ phalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Madana</s> is emetic; it is called <s>Rāṭha</s>, <s>Piṇḍī</s>, <s>Piṇḍītaka</s>, and <s>Phala</s>.
It is also <s>Tagara</s>, <s>Karahāṭa</s>, <s>Śalyaka</s>, and <s>Viṣapuṣpaka</s>.
It is likewise <s>Snehapiṇḍītaka</s>, and is specifically a cleanser of the bladder.

children.text: chardano vāmanaścaiva sa ca gālaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is called <s>Chardana</s> and <s>Vāmana</s>, and it is also proclaimed as <s>Gāla</s>.
<s>Madana</s> causes vomiting and removes difficulty in vomiting, ear disorders, wounds, and discharges.
It is dry and removes skin disease, kapha, abdominal distension, swelling, tumors, and wounds.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭhaka</s>, <s>Kākakuṣṭha</s>, <s>Recana</s>, and <s>Raṅganāyaka</s>,
<s>Varāṅga</s>, <s>Pupulaka</s>, <s>Hāsa</s>, <s>Śodhana</s>, and <s>Kiñjavāluka</s> are its names.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is purgative, bitter, pungent, hot, and improves the complexion.
It removes worms, swelling, abdominal disease, distension, tumors, obstruction, and kapha.
<s>Hemāhvā</s>, <s>Kanakakṣīrī</s>, <s>Hemakṣīrī</s>, and <s>Kāñcanī</s>,
<s>Kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>Kāñcanakṣīrī</s>, <s>Kaṭuparṇī</s>, and <s>Karṣiṇī</s>,
<s>Tiktā</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Dugdhā</s>, <s>Hemadugdhā</s>, and <s>Himāvatī</s>,
<s>Svarṇakṣīrī</s>, <s>Svarṇadugdhā</s>, and also <s>Suvarṇakṣīrikā</s>,
<s>Pītadugdhā</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Tiktadugdhā</s>, and <s>Himādrijā</s> are names.
<s>Hemāhvā</s> is purgative, bitter, intoxicating, and causes nausea or agitation.
It destroys worms, pallor, kapha, obstruction, poison, and skin disease.

children.text: sātalā saptalā sārā vidulā vimalā matā
children.translated_text: <s>Sātalā</s>, <s>Saptalā</s>, <s>Sārā</s>, <s>Vidulā</s>, and <s>Vimalā</s> are recognized as its names.

children.text: bahuphenā carmakasā phenā dīptā tu nālikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bahuphenā</s>, <s>Carmakasā</s>, <s>Phenā</s>, <s>Dīptā</s>, and <s>Nālikā</s> are also used.

children.text: sātalā kaṭukā pāke vātalā śītalā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sātalā</s> is pungent in digestion, vāta-producing, cooling, and light.
It is bitter and conquers swelling, kapha, obstruction, pitta, upward movement of vāta, and blood disorders.
<s>Aśmantaka</s> is <s>Yugmapattra</s>, <s>Kuśalī</s>, and <s>Pāpanāśana</s>.

children.text: ślakṣmatvag aśmayoniḥ syāt pāṣāṇāntaka eva ca ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>Ślakṣmatvak</s>, <s>Aśmayoni</s>, and also <s>Pāṣāṇāntaka</s>.
A second <s>Aśmantaka</s> is also remembered as otherwise with respect to its qualities.
<s>Aśmanta</s> is astringent, binding, both cold and hot, and conquers kapha and vāta.
It destroys goiter, bleeding swellings, scrofula, and diseases of the throat.
Its fruit is scraping, binding, heavy, and removes phlegm and wind.

children.text: tanmaṣī śastraghāte tu śreṣṭhā ca vraṇaropaṇe ||
children.translated_text: Its ash is excellent for weapon wounds and for healing sores.
<s>Kāñcanāra</s> is <s>Kāñcanaka</s>, <s>Pākārī</s>, and <s>Raktapuṣpaka</s>.
<s>Kovidāra</s> is a variety of it; it is <s>Kuddāla</s>, <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>, and <s>Kulī</s>.
It is <s>Tāmrapuṣpa</s>, <s>Camarika</s>, and <s>Mahāyamalapattraka</s>.
It is <s>Āsphota</s>, <s>Uddālaka</s>, <s>Svalpakeśara</s>, and <s>Kulāhala</s>.
<s>Kāñcanāra</s> is cold, binding, astringent, and conquers phlegm and pitta.
It removes worms, skin disease, rectal prolapse, scrofula, and wounds.
<s>Kovidāra</s> too is the same; the flower of both is cold and light.
It is dry, binding, and removes pitta, blood disorders, leucorrhea, wasting injury, and cough.
<s>Nirguṇḍī</s>, with white flowers, is <s>Sinduka</s> and <s>Sinduvāraka</s>.
It is <s>Bhūtakeśī</s>; another is <s>Nīlasinduka</s>, with blue flowers, and <s>Śephālikā</s>.
It is <s>Śītabhīru</s>, <s>Varṇaka</s>, and <s>Nīlamañjarī</s>.

children.text: nirguṇḍī smṛtidā tiktā kaṣāyā kaṭukā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nirguṇḍī</s> gives memory; it is bitter, astringent, pungent, and light.
It benefits the hair and eyes and removes pain, swelling, undigested matter, and wind.
It removes worms, skin disease, vāta, phlegm, wounds, anorexia, and poison.
<s>Ajaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and <s>Sarpadaṃṣṭrā</s> are named.
It is <s>Tiktadugdhā</s>, a medicine for the eyes, <s>Putraśreṇī</s>, and <s>Viṣāṇikā</s>.
It is regarded as <s>Vṛścikālī</s>; others call it <s>Trapusī</s>.
<s>Uṣṭrī</s>, <s>Lomaśapuṣpā</s>, <s>Dhīvṛkṣā</s>, and <s>Ghanaśṛṅgikā</s>,

children.text: viṣaghnā pādavṛkṣaśca kālī cakṣuṣya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣaghnā</s>, <s>Pādavṛkṣa</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, and <s>Cakṣuṣyā</s> are its names.
<s>Vāmāvartā</s>, <s>Viṣaharī</s>, <s>Kālikā</s>, and <s>Netrabheṣajā</s>,
<s>Sakṣīrā</s>, <s>Karkaśā</s>, <s>Yugmaphalā</s>, and <s>Uttaravāhinī</s> are also names.
<s>Māṣaparṇī</s>, <s>Alparomā</s>, and <s>Meṣavallī</s> are declared.
A second kind is <s>Dakṣiṇāvartā</s>, <s>Vṛścikālī</s>, and <s>Viṣāṇikā</s>.
Another <s>Vṛścikā</s> is <s>Pattrī</s> and also <s>Carmakavṛntikā</s>.
It is <s>Badarā</s>, <s>Meghapuṣpā</s>, and likewise <s>Bhāsurapuṣpikā</s>.
<s>Vṛścikālī</s> conquers cough, pacifies vāta, and removes poison.
<s>Punarnavā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Raktapuṣpā</s>, and <s>Śivāṭikā</s>,
<s>Krūraka</s>, <s>Kṣudravarṣābhū</s>, <s>Dīrghapattra</s>, and <s>Kṣudraka</s> are its names.

children.text: punarnavā sarā tiktā rūkṣoṣṇā madhurā kaṭuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Punarnavā</s> is flowing, bitter, dry, hot, sweet, and pungent.
It removes swelling, wind, wounds, and phlegm; it promotes appetite and is rejuvenative.
Red <s>Punarnavā</s> is bitter, red-flowered, and called <s>Kaṭhillaka</s>.
It is <s>Krūraka</s>, <s>Kṣudravarṣābhū</s>, <s>Varṣaketu</s>, and <s>Śivāṭikā</s>.
Red <s>Punarnavā</s> is bitter, pungent in digestion, cold, and light.
It produces vāta, is binding, and destroys phlegm, blood disorders, and abscesses.
<s>Rāsnā</s>, <s>Raktā</s>, <s>Yuktarasā</s>, <s>Rasanā</s>, and <s>Gandhanākulī</s>,
<s>Sugandhimūlā</s>, <s>Atirasā</s>, <s>Śreyasī</s>, <s>Subahā</s>, and <s>Rasā</s> are its names.
<s>Rāsnā</s> is digestive, bitter, heavy, hot, and conquers phlegm and vāta.
It removes swelling, dyspnea, wind, blood disorders, vāta-related swelling, and abdominal disease.
<s>Aśvagandhā</s> is <s>Turaṅgāhvā</s>, <s>Gokarṇā</s>, and <s>Aśvāvarohaka</s>.
It is <s>Vārāhakarṇī</s>, <s>Varadā</s>, strengthening, aphrodisiac, and virilizing.
<s>Aśvagandhā</s> removes wind, phlegm, swelling, white leprosy, and wasting disease.
It is strengthening, rejuvenative, bitter, astringent, hot, and very semen-promoting.
<s>Prasāriṇī</s> is <s>Rājabalā</s>, <s>Cāruparṇī</s>, and <s>Pratānikā</s>.
It is <s>Saraṇī</s>, <s>Sāraṇī</s>, <s>Bhadraparṇī</s>, <s>Suprasarā</s>, and <s>Sarā</s>.
<s>Prasāriṇī</s> is heavy, aphrodisiac, restores the joints of the eyelids, and is flowing.
It is hot in potency, removes vāta, is bitter, and removes vātarakta and kapha.
<s>Śatāvarī</s> is <s>Dvīpiśatru</s>, <s>Dvīpikā</s>, <s>Dharakaṇṭakā</s>,
<s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, <s>Śatapadī</s>, <s>Śatāhvā</s>, and <s>Bahupattrikā</s>.

children.text: śatāvarī guruḥ śītā svāduḥ snigdhā rasāyanī
children.translated_text: <s>Śatāvarī</s> is heavy, cold, sweet, unctuous, and rejuvenative.
It produces semen and breast milk, is strengthening, and conquers vāta, pitta, blood disorders, and swelling.
Another <s>Śatāvarī</s>, with upward thorns, is <s>Pīvarī</s> and <s>Indīvarī</s>.
It is <s>Abhīru</s>, <s>Bahupattrā</s>, and <s>Mahāpuruṣadantikā</s>.
It is <s>Sahasravīryā</s> and <s>Keśī</s>; <s>Tuṅginī</s> is <s>Sūkṣmapattrikā</s>.
Great <s>Śatāvarī</s> is intellect-promoting, cordial, and rejuvenative.
Cold in potency, it destroys piles, grahaṇī disease, and diseases of the eyes.
<s>Balā</s> is <s>Vāṭyālakā</s>, <s>Śītapākī</s>, and called <s>Vāṭyodanā</s>.
It is <s>Bhadraudanī</s>, <s>Samaṅgā</s>, <s>Samāṃśā</s>, and <s>Kharayaṣṭikā</s>.
<s>Mahābalā</s> is <s>Vīrapuṣpī</s>, <s>Sahadevī</s>, and <s>Bṛhadbalā</s>.
It is <s>Vāṭyāyinī</s>, <s>Devasahā</s>, <s>Vāṭyā</s>, and <s>Pītapuṣpikā</s>.
It is <s>Gandhavarṇā</s>, <s>Mahāgandhā</s>, <s>Varṣāpuṣpā</s>, and <s>Prasādinī</s>.
<s>Bālikā</s>, <s>Atibalā</s>, and <s>Bhāradvājī</s> are names; it is <s>Akṣagandhinī</s>.
<s>Gāṅgerukī</s>, <s>Nāgabalā</s>, <s>Viśvedevā</s>, and <s>Gavedhukā</s> are names.
The four <s>Balā</s> plants are cold, sweet, strengthening, and complexion-promoting.
They are unctuous and binding, and destroy wind, blood disorders, catarrh, and wasting injury.
Among these, <s>Bṛhadbalā</s> removes dysuria and directs vāta downward.
<s>Nāgabalā</s> is heavy, aphrodisiac, and especially conquers raktapitta.
It is strengthening, rejuvenative, virility-increasing, and also nourishing.

children.text: tasyāḥ phalaṃ himaṃ svādustambhanaṃ guru lekhanam
children.translated_text: Its fruit is cold, sweet, restraining, heavy, and scraping.
It causes constipation and distension and removes raktapitta.
<s>Tejasvinī</s>, <s>Tejavatī</s>, <s>Tejinī</s>, and <s>Alaghuvalkalā</s>,
<s>Mahaujasī</s>, <s>Pārijātā</s>, <s>Śītā</s>, <s>Tiktā</s>, and <s>Atitejinī</s> are its names.
<s>Tejasvinī</s> conquers phlegm, dyspnea, cough, diseases of the mouth, and vāta.
It is digestive, hot, pungent and bitter, and kindles taste and digestive fire.
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> is <s>Vahniruci</s>, <s>Kaṅganī</s>, and also <s>Kaṭabhī</s>.
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> is pungent, bitter, flowing, and conquers phlegm and vāta.
It is very hot, subduing, sharp, and gives digestive fire, intellect, and memory.
<s>Devadāru</s> is <s>Surāhva</s>, <s>Bhadradāru</s>, and <s>Suradruma</s>.
It is <s>Bhadrakāṣṭha</s>, <s>Snehavṛkṣa</s>, <s>Kilima</s>, and <s>Śakradāru</s>.
<s>Devadāru</s> is pungent, unctuous, bitter, hot, and light; it removes
distension, fever, wasting, undigested matter, hiccup, itching, phlegm, and vāta.
<s>Sarala</s> is <s>Nandana</s>, <s>Cīḍa</s>, <s>Nameru</s>, and <s>Darpivṛkṣaka</s>.
It is <s>Pītadāru</s>, <s>Pītavṛkṣa</s>, <s>Mahādīrgha</s>, and <s>Kalidruma</s>.

children.text: saralaḥ kaṭukaḥ pāke rasato madhuro laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sarala</s> is pungent in digestion, sweet in taste, and light.
It is hot and unctuous, and removes diseases of vāta, eyes, throat, and ears.
<s>Puṣkarāhva</s>, <s>Padmapattra</s>, <s>Pauṣkara</s>, and <s>Puṣkarāṅghrika</s>,
<s>Kāśmīra</s>, <s>Puṣkarajaṭā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, and <s>Sugandhika</s> are its names.
<s>Pauṣkara</s> is pungent, bitter, and hot; it destroys vāta, kapha, and fevers.
It removes swelling, anorexia, and dyspnea, and especially conquers pain in the side.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s> is <s>Rogāhvaya</s>, <s>Vāpya</s>, <s>Kaubera</s>, and <s>Pāribhadraka</s>.
It is <s>Pārihārya</s>, <s>Pāribhāvya</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, and <s>Haribhadraka</s>.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s> is hot, pungent, sweet, semen-producing, and light.
It destroys vāta, blood disorders, erysipelas, cough, skin disease, vāta, and phlegm.
<s>Śṛṅgī</s> is <s>Kulīraśṛṅgī</s>, <s>Vakrā</s>, and <s>Karkaṭaśṛṅgikā</s>.
It is called <s>Karkaṭā</s>, <s>Mahāghoṣā</s>, <s>Śṛṅganāmnī</s>, and also <s>Natāṅgī</s>.
<s>Śṛṅgī</s> is astringent, bitter, and hot; it removes hiccup, vomiting, and fever.
It removes thirst, dizziness, phlegm, dyspnea, wasting, cough, and upward-moving vāta.

children.text: rohiṣaṃ kattṛṇam bhūtir bhūtīkaṃ saralaṃ tṛṇam
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṣa</s> is <s>Kattṛṇa</s>, <s>Bhūti</s>, <s>Bhūtīka</s>, <s>Sarala</s>, and <s>Tṛṇa</s>.
It is <s>Śyāmala</s>, <s>Yugdala</s>, <s>Paura</s>, <s>Dhyāmaka</s>, and <s>Devagandhaka</s>.

children.text: rohiṣaṃ kaṭukam pāke tiktoṣṇaṃ tuvaraṃ jayet
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṣa</s> is pungent in digestion, bitter, hot, and astringent; it conquers
diseases of the throat and heart, pitta, blood disorders, colic, cough, phlegm, and fever.
<s>Kaṭphala</s> is <s>Kumudā</s>, <s>Kumbhī</s>, <s>Śrīparṇī</s>, and <s>Somapādapa</s>.
It is <s>Somavalka</s>, <s>Mahākumbhī</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Bhadravatī</s>, and <s>Śivā</s>.
<s>Kaṭphala</s> is astringent, bitter, and pungent; it destroys vāta, kapha, and fever.
It removes dyspnea, urinary disorders, piles, cough, throat disease, and anorexia.
<s>Bhārṅgī</s> is <s>Bhṛgubhavā</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, <s>Kāsaghnī</s>, and foremost among <s>Bhārgava</s> plants.
It is <s>Kharaśāka</s>, <s>Śukramātā</s>, <s>Phañjī</s>, and <s>Brāhmaṇayaṣṭikā</s>.

children.text: bhārṅgī rūkṣā kaṭustiktā rucyoṣṇā pācanī jayet
children.translated_text: <s>Bhārṅgī</s> is dry, pungent, bitter, tasteful, hot, and digestive; it conquers
swelling, dyspnea, wind, blood disorders, catarrh, fever, and vāta.
<s>Pāṣāṇabheda</s> is <s>Pāṣāṇa</s>, <s>Aśmarībheda</s>, and <s>Aśmabhedaka</s>.
It is <s>Śilābheda</s>, <s>Dṛṣadbheda</s>, <s>Nagabhinna</s>, and <s>Nagabhedana</s>.
<s>Pāṣāṇabheda</s> is astringent, cold, and cleansing for the bladder.
It is flowing and bitter, and conquers urinary disease, piles, dysuria, urinary stones, and pain.
<s>Musta</s> is <s>Vāridhara</s>, <s>Mustā</s>, <s>Meghākhya</s>, and <s>Kuruvindaka</s>.
It is <s>Varāha</s>, <s>Abda</s>, <s>Ghana</s>, <s>Bhadramusta</s>, and <s>Rājakaseruka</s>.
<s>Piṇḍamusta</s> is another, known as <s>Viṣadhvaṃsī</s> and <s>Nāgara</s>.

children.text: mustaṃ kaṭu himaṃ grāhi tiktaṃ dīpanapācanam
children.translated_text: <s>Musta</s> is pungent, cold, binding, bitter, and kindles and digests.
It is astringent and removes worms, pitta, blood disorders, phlegm, thirst, and fever.
<s>Dhātakī</s> is <s>Kuñjarā</s>, <s>Sindhupuṣpī</s>, <s>Pramadinī</s>, and <s>Madā</s>.
It is <s>Pārvatīyā</s>, <s>Tāmrapuṣpī</s>, <s>Subhikṣā</s>, and <s>Madyavāsinī</s>.

children.text: dhātakī kaṭukā śītā madakṛt tuvarā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātakī</s> is pungent, cold, intoxicating, astringent, and light.
It conquers thirst, diarrhea, pitta, blood disorders, poison, worms, and erysipelas.
<s>Mācikā</s> is <s>Bālikā</s>, <s>Ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śacī</s>, and <s>Dantaśaṭhāmbikā</s>.
It is <s>Āmbaṣṭhakī</s>, <s>Sūcimukhī</s>, astringent, and <s>Kaṭaṃmukhī</s>.

children.text: mācikāmlā rase pāke kaṣāyā śītalā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mācikā</s> is sour in taste and digestion, astringent, cold, and light.
It removes chronic diarrhea, pitta, blood disorders, phlegm, and throat disease.
<s>Vidārikā</s> is <s>Vṛṣyavallī</s>, <s>Vṛṣyakandā</s>, and <s>Vidālikā</s>.

It is <s>Ikṣuvallī</s>, <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, <s>Kṣīragandhā</s>, and <s>Ikṣugandhikā</s>.
<s>Vidārī</s> is sweet, unctuous, nourishing, and gives breast milk and semen.
It is heavy, removes pitta, blood disorders, vāta, and burning, and is rejuvenative.
<s>Vārāhī</s> is <s>Mādhavī</s>, <s>Ghṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Saukarī</s>, and <s>Vanamālikā</s>.
Its tuber is called <s>Kiṭi</s>, <s>Kroḍanāmā</s>, and <s>Śambarakandaka</s>.
<s>Vārāhī</s> is sweet in its tuber, pungent, bitter, and very semen-promoting.
It is strengthening and pitta-producing, and conquers vāta, kapha, pitta, and worms.
<s>Pāṭhā</s> is <s>Ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>Bṛhattiktā</s>, <s>Prācīnāmbaṣṭhakī</s>, and <s>Rasā</s>.
It is <s>Varā</s>, bitter, <s>Pāpacelī</s>, <s>Śreyasī</s>, and <s>Viddhakarṇikā</s>.
<s>Pāṭhā</s> is hot, pungent, sharp, removing vāta and phlegm, and light.
It destroys colic, fever, vomiting, skin disease, diarrhea, and heart pain,
as well as burning, itching, poison, dyspnea, worms, abdominal tumors, abdominal disease, and wounds.
<s>Mūrvā</s> is <s>Devī</s>, <s>Madhurasā</s>, <s>Devaśreṇī</s>, and <s>Madhusravā</s>.
