<s>Mūrvā</s> is flowing, heavy, sweet and bitter; it removes pitta, blood disorders, and urinary disease.
It removes the three doṣas, thirst, heart disease, itching, skin disease, and fever.
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> is <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Raktā</s>, <s>Raktāṅgī</s>, and <s>Kālameṣikā</s>.
It is <s>Raktayaṣṭī</s>, <s>Tāmravallī</s>, <s>Samaṅgā</s>, and <s>Vastrabhūṣaṇā</s>.
It is <s>Mañjulā</s>, <s>Vikasā</s>, <s>Bhaṇḍī</s>, <s>Chadmikā</s>, and <s>Jvaranāśinī</s>.
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> is sweet, bitter, astringent, and improves voice and complexion.
It is heavy and hot, and conquers poison, phlegm, swelling, and pain of the womb and eyes.
It removes bloody diarrhea, skin disease, blood disorders, erysipelas, wounds, and urinary disease.
Its greens kindle digestion, are sweet and unctuous, and remove pitta and wind.
<s>Haridrā</s> is <s>Rajanī</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Rañjinī</s>, and <s>Varavarṇinī</s>.
It is <s>Piṇḍī</s>, <s>Pītā</s>, <s>Varṇavatī</s>, <s>Niśā</s>, and <s>Haṭṭavilāsinī</s>.
<s>Haridrā</s> is pungent, bitter, dry, hot, and removes phlegm and pitta.
It improves complexion and removes skin disorders, urinary disease, blood disorders, swelling, jaundice, and wounds.
<s>Dārvī</s> is another <s>Dāruharidrā</s>, <s>Pītadāru</s>, and <s>Pacampacā</s>.
It is <s>Kaṭaṅkaṭerī</s>, <s>Pītadru</s>, <s>Svarṇavarṇā</s>, and <s>Kaṭaṃkaṭī</s>.
<s>Dārvī</s> is like that, but especially conquers diseases of the eyes, ears, and mouth.
<s>Prapunnāṭa</s> is <s>Eḍagaja</s>, <s>Cakramarda</s>, and <s>Prapunnaṭa</s>.
It is <s>Dadrughna</s>, <s>Mardaka</s>, <s>Meṣakusuma</s>, and <s>Kuṣṭhakṛntana</s>.
<s>Prapunnāṭa</s> is light, sweet, dry, and removes pitta and wind.
It is good for the heart, cold, and conquers phlegm, dyspnea, skin disease, ringworm, and worms.
Its fruit, being hot, destroys skin disease, ringworm, itching, poison, and wind.
Its greens remove vātarakta; they remove phlegm and are light.
<s>Bākucī</s> is <s>Candrikā</s>, <s>Somavallī</s>, <s>Pūtiphalā</s>, and <s>Varā</s>.
It is <s>Somarājī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaphalā</s>, <s>Avalgujā</s>, and <s>Kālameṣikā</s>.
<s>Vākucī</s> is sweet and bitter, pungent in digestion, and rejuvenative.
It is constipating, cold, appetizing, flowing, good for the heart, and removes blood-pitta.
It is dry and destroys phlegm, dyspnea, skin disease, urinary disease, fever, and worms.
Its fruit produces pitta and removes white leprosy, vāta, and kapha.
<s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s> is <s>Bhekarāja</s>, <s>Mārkava</s>, and <s>Keśarañjana</s>.
It is <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgaraja</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgāhva</s>, and <s>Sūryavallabha</s>.
<s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s> is pungent, bitter, dry, hot, and conquers kapha and vāta.
It cleanses the teeth, is rejuvenative and appetizing, and removes skin disease and pains of the eyes and head.
<s>Parpaṭa</s> is <s>Kavaca</s>, <s>Reṇu</s>, <s>Pittahā</s>, and <s>Yavakaṇṭaka</s>.
It is <s>Vara</s>, bitter, <s>Parpaṭaka</s>, <s>Pṛthvikā</s>, and <s>Carmakaṇṭaka</s>.
<s>Parpaṭa</s> destroys pitta, blood disorders, dizziness, thirst, kapha, and fever.
It is binding, cold, bitter, removes burning, produces vāta, and is light.
<s>Śaṇapuṣpī</s> is <s>Mālyapuṣpī</s>, <s>Dhāvanī</s>, and <s>Śaṇaghaṇṭikā</s>.
It is <s>Bṛhatpuṣpī</s>, <s>Svalpaghaṇṭā</s>, <s>Ghaṇṭāśabdā</s>, and <s>Urupuṣpikā</s>.
<s>Śaṇapuṣpī</s> is pungent, conquers pitta and phlegm, and causes vomiting.
<s>Trāyamāṇā</s> is <s>Suratrāṇā</s>, <s>Trāyantī</s>, and <s>Girisānujā</s>.
It is <s>Balabhadrā</s>, <s>Kṛtatrāṇā</s>, <s>Vārṣika</s>, and <s>Trāyamāṇaka</s>.
<s>Trāyamāṇā</s> is flowing and conquers pitta-fever, phlegm, blood disorders, and pain.
<s>Mahājālinikā</s> is <s>Carmaraṅgā</s> and should be <s>Pītakīlikā</s>.
It is <s>Āvartakī</s>, <s>Bindukinī</s>, <s>Vibhāṇḍī</s>, and <s>Raktapuṣpikā</s>.
<s>Mahājālinikā</s> is bitter, purgative, and conquers kapha and pitta.
It destroys burning, abdominal disease, distension, swelling, skin disease, worms, and fever.
<s>Ativiṣā</s> is <s>Śuklakandā</s>, <s>Viṣā</s>, <s>Prativiṣā</s>, and <s>Parā</s>.
It is <s>Śyāmakandā</s>, <s>Asitā</s>, <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Bhaṅgurā</s>, and <s>Upaviṣāṇikā</s>.
<s>Viṣā</s> is hot, digestive, bitter, and conquers phlegm, vāta, and diarrhea.
<s>Kākamācī</s> is <s>Dhvāṅkṣamācī</s>, <s>Kāmācī</s>, and <s>Jaghanephalā</s>.
It is rejuvenative, excellent, very bitter, and should be <s>Kākinī</s> and pungent.
<s>Kākamācī</s> destroys the three doṣas, is unctuous and hot, and gives voice and semen.
It is good for the heart, rejuvenative, and conquers swelling, skin disease, piles, fever, and urinary disease.
<s>Kākajaṅghā</s> is <s>Nadīkāntā</s>, <s>Kākatiktā</s>, and <s>Salomaśā</s>.
It is <s>Pārāvatapadī</s>, <s>Kākā</s>, <s>Madadhyā</s>, and also <s>Karmaṇī</s>.
<s>Kākajaṅghā</s> is cold and destroys blood-pitta, kapha, and fever.
<s>Lodhra</s> is <s>Tirīṭa</s>, <s>Kānīna</s>, <s>Tilvaka</s>, and <s>Saṃtatodbhava</s>.
Another is <s>Ghanatvak</s>, <s>Śabara</s>, <s>Śvetalodhra</s>, a medicine for the eyes.
<s>Lodhra</s> is purgative, cold, good for the eyes, and removes kapha and pitta.
It is astringent and destroys blood disorders, swelling, blood disease, fever, and diarrhea.
Its flower is sweet, binding, slightly bitter, and conquers phlegm and pitta.
<s>Vṛddhadāru</s> is <s>Mahāśyāma</s>, <s>Jāṅgala</s>, and <s>Vṛddhadāruka</s>.
It should be <s>Antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī</s>, <s>Āvegī</s>, and <s>Chagalāntrikā</s>.
<s>Vṛddhadāru</s> is astringent, hot, flowing, bitter, and rejuvenative.
It is aphrodisiac and conquers vāta, rheumatism, blood disorders, swelling, urinary disease, and kapha.
<s>Devadālī</s> is <s>Vṛttakośā</s>, <s>Devatāḍa</s>, and <s>Garāgarī</s>.
It is <s>Jīmūta</s>, <s>Tāḍakā</s>, <s>Veṇī</s>, <s>Jālinī</s>, and removes rat poison.
<s>Devadālī</s> is bitter in taste and destroys kapha, piles, swelling, and jaundice.
It is emetic and sharp, and destroys wasting disease, hiccup, worms, and fever.
<s>Haṃsapādī</s> is <s>Haṃsapadī</s>, <s>Raktapādī</s>, and <s>Nṛpādikā</s>.
It is <s>Prahlādanī</s>, <s>Kīṭamārī</s>, <s>Kīṭamātā</s>, and <s>Madhusravā</s>.
<s>Haṃsapādī</s> is heavy and cold; it removes blood disorders, poison, and wounds.
It is healing, and removes erysipelas, burning, diarrhea, spiders' poison, and disorders from spirits.
<s>Nākulī</s> is <s>Suvahā</s>, <s>Sarpagandhinī</s>, and <s>Gandhanākulī</s>.
It is regarded as <s>Nakuleṣṭā</s>, <s>Sarpanetrā</s>, and <s>Cīritapattrikā</s>.
<s>Nākulī</s> is astringent, bitter, pungent, and hot; it destroys
the poison of spiders, scorpions, mice, and snakes, as well as worms and wounds.
<s>Vaṭapattrī</s> is digestive; it is considered intoxicating and purgative.
<s>Vaṭapattrī</s>, being astringent and hot, destroys diseases of the female genital tract.
Its fruit is constipating, cold, vāta-producing, and conquers phlegm and pitta.
<s>Lajjālu</s> is <s>Medinī</s>, <s>Spṛkkā</s>, <s>Khādirī</s>, and <s>Gandhakāriṇī</s>.
It is <s>Namakārī</s>, <s>Śamīpattrā</s>, <s>Samaṅgā</s>, and <s>Raktapādikā</s>.
<s>Lajjālu</s> is cold, bitter, and astringent; it conquers phlegm and pitta.
It destroys bleeding disorders, diarrhea, and diseases of the female genital tract.
<s>Somavallī</s> is <s>Yajñanetā</s>, <s>Somakṣīrī</s>, and dear to twice-born men.
<s>Somavallī</s> removes the three doṣas, is pungent and bitter, and is rejuvenative.
<s>Musalī</s> is <s>Khalinī</s>, <s>Tālapatrī</s>, and <s>Kāñcanapuṣpikā</s>.
It is highly aphrodisiac, <s>Vṛṣyakandā</s>, <s>Kharjūrī</s>, and <s>Tālamūlikā</s>.

children.text: musalī madhurā vṛṣyā vīryoṣṇā bṛṃhaṇī guruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Musalī</s> is sweet, aphrodisiac, hot in potency, nourishing, and heavy.
It is bitter and rejuvenative, and removes rectal disease and wind there as well.
<s>Kapikacchu</s> is <s>Svayaṅguptā</s>, <s>Kaṇḍūrā</s>, and hard to seize.
It is <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Ātmaguptā</s>, <s>Lāṅgūlī</s>, <s>Markaṭī</s>, and also <s>Harṣiṇī</s>.

children.text: kapikacchuḥ paraṃ vṛṣyā madhurā bṛṃhaṇī guruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kapikacchu</s> is supremely aphrodisiac, sweet, nourishing, and heavy.
Its seed pacifies vāta and is an excellent virilizing agent.
<s>Putrajīva</s> produces conception; it is <s>Yaṣṭipuṣpa</s> and <s>Arthasādhana</s>.
<s>Putrajīva</s> is heavy, aphrodisiac, and conception-giving, but produces phlegm and vāta.
<s>Vandhyākarkoṭikā</s> is <s>Devī</s>, <s>Kumārī</s>, and destroyer of poison.
It is remembered as <s>Manojñā</s>, <s>Nāgadamanī</s>, <s>Vandhyā</s>, and <s>Yogeśvarī</s>.
<s>Vandhyākarkoṭikā</s> is light, removes phlegm, and cleanses wounds.
It breaks the pride of snakes, is sharp, and wards off erysipelas and poison.
<s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s> is <s>Nīlapuṣpī</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Vaśyā</s>, and <s>Aparājitā</s>.
<s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s> is pungent and intellect-promoting; it conquers worms, wounds, and phlegm.
<s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> is <s>Śaṅkhanāmnī</s>, <s>Kirīṭī</s>, and <s>Kambumālinī</s>.
It is <s>Kambupuṣpī</s>, beneficial for memory, intellect-promoting, and delighting in the forest.
<s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> is flowing and intellect-promoting, and is considered not to derange the mind.
It is rejuvenative, astringent, hot, and destroys disorders of memory and urinary disease.
<s>Dugdhikā</s> is <s>Madhuparṇī</s>, <s>Kṣīriṇī</s>, and <s>Svādupuṣpikā</s>.
It is <s>Kṣudraparṇī</s>, <s>Payasyā</s>, remover of urinary disease, and <s>Madhucchadā</s>.
It is <s>Nāgārjunī</s>, <s>Nāgasahā</s>, <s>Kumāratilakā</s>, and <s>Parā</s>.
<s>Dugdhikā</s> is hot, heavy, dry, vāta-producing, and conception-producing.
It is sweet, obstructive, aphrodisiac, and conquers phlegm, skin disease, and worms.
<s>Arkapuṣpī</s> is <s>Krūrakarmā</s>, <s>Jalakāmā</s>, and <s>Bhiriṇḍikā</s>.
<s>Arkapuṣpī</s> removes worms, phlegm, urinary disease, and disorders of the mind.
<s>Bhallātaka</s> is <s>Anala</s>, <s>Bhallī</s>, <s>Vīravṛkṣa</s>, and <s>Agnivaktraka</s>.
It is <s>Aruṣkara</s>, <s>Aruṣka</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Agnimukhī</s>, and <s>Dhanuḥ</s>.
<s>Bhallātaka</s> is astringent, hot, semen-promoting, sweet, and light.
It removes vāta, phlegm, abdominal disease, distension, skin disease, piles, and grahaṇī disorders.
It removes abdominal tumors, fever, white leprosy, weak digestion, worms, and wounds.
<s>Cirapoṭā</s> is <s>Dīrghapatrā</s>, <s>Kuntala</s>, and is regarded as <s>Tiktakā</s>.
<s>Cirapoṭā</s> is cold, dry, splitting, and conquers dyspnea and cough.
<s>Droṇapuṣpī</s> is <s>Śvasanakā</s>, <s>Pālindī</s>, and <s>Kumbhayonikā</s>.
It is <s>Chattrā</s>, <s>Atichattrikā</s>, <s>Droṇā</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, and <s>Vṛkṣasāraka</s>.
<s>Droṇapuṣpī</s> is heavy, dry, sweet, hot, and removes vāta and pitta.
It is splitting, and removes jaundice, swelling, phlegm, and worms; it is light.
<s>Brāhmī</s> is <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Somā</s>, <s>Satyāhvā</s>, and <s>Brahmacāriṇī</s>.
It is <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>Māṇḍūkī</s>, <s>Tvāṣṭrī</s>, <s>Divyā</s>, and <s>Mahauṣadhī</s>.
It is <s>Kapotavaṅkā</s>, <s>Munikā</s>, <s>Lāvaṇyā</s>, and <s>Somavallarī</s>.

children.text: brāhmī sarā himā svādurlaghur medhyā rasāyanī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmī</s> is flowing, cold, sweet, light, intellect-promoting, and rejuvenative.
It benefits the voice, gives memory, and conquers skin disease, anemia, urinary disease, blood disorders, and cough.
It removes poison, swelling, and fever; <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇinī</s> is the same in that respect.
<s>Suvarcalā</s> is <s>Arkakāntā</s>, <s>Sūryabhaktā</s>, and <s>Sukhodbhavā</s>.
It is <s>Sūryāvartā</s> and <s>Raviprītā</s>; another is <s>Brahmasuvarcalā</s>.
<s>Suvarcalā</s> is heavy, cold, diuretic, and conquers phlegm and vāta.
The other is hot, removes skin disease, urinary disease, stone, dysuria, and fever, and is light.
<s>Matsyākṣī</s> is <s>Bāhlikā</s>, <s>Matsyagandhī</s>, and likewise <s>Matsyādanī</s>.
<s>Matsyākṣī</s> is binding and bitter; it removes skin disease, pitta, phlegm, and blood disorders.
<s>Jalapippalī</s> is <s>Ambuvallī</s>, <s>Pattūra</s>, and also <s>Kañcaṭa</s>.
<s>Jalapippalikā</s> benefits the heart and eyes, promotes semen, and is light.
It is binding, cold, dry, and removes bleeding, burning, and wounds.
<s>Gojihvā</s> is <s>Gojikā</s>, <s>Gobhī</s>, <s>Dīrghikā</s>, and <s>Kharaparṇinī</s>.
<s>Gojihvā</s> produces vāta, is cold and binding, and removes phlegm and pitta.
It benefits the heart and removes urinary disease, cough, blood disorders, wounds, and fever; it is light.
<s>Nāgāhvā</s> is <s>Damanī</s>, <s>Nāgagandhā</s>, and <s>Bhujagaparṇinī</s>.
It is <s>Nāgadamanī</s>, good for wounds, and removes poison from spiders and snakes.
<s>Guñjā</s> is <s>Śikhaṇḍikā</s>, <s>Tāmrā</s>, <s>Raktikā</s>, and <s>Kākaṇantikā</s>.
The white variety is <s>Cakrikā</s>, <s>Cūḍā</s>, <s>Durmukhī</s>, and <s>Kākapīlukā</s>.
<s>Guñjā</s> benefits the hair, gives strength, benefits the skin, and removes pitta and phlegm.
It removes diseases of the eyes, itching, graha afflictions, and wounds.
It removes worms, hair loss, and skin diseases; the white variety is especially praised in the same way.
<s>Vellantara</s> is <s>Dīrghapatra</s>, <s>Vīradru</s>, and <s>Bahupattraka</s>.
<s>Vellantara</s> checks upward movement and conquers phlegm, dysuria, and pain from vāta.
<s>Vandāka</s> is also <s>Vṛkṣaruhā</s>, <s>Śekharī</s>, and <s>Kāmavṛkṣaka</s>.
It is <s>Vṛkṣādanī</s>, <s>Kāmataru</s>, <s>Kāminī</s>, and <s>Pādarohiṇī</s>.
<s>Vandāka</s> removes phlegm, vāta, blood disorders, pulmonary disease, wounds, and poison.
<s>Piṇḍāra</s> is <s>Karahāṭa</s>, <s>Tīkṣṇakīla</s>, and <s>Kuraṅgaka</s>.
<s>Piṇḍāra</s> is sweet and cold, and removes swelling, pitta, and phlegm.
<s>Chikkikā</s> is <s>Kṣavaka</s>, harsh, nose-irritating, and pungent.
<s>Chikkikā</s> is pittala and removes skin disease, worms, vāta, and phlegm.
<s>Rohita</s>, <s>Dāḍimīpuṣpa</s>, <s>Rohīta</s>, and <s>Kūṭaśālmali</s>,
<s>Plīhā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Rohī</s>, <s>Raktaghna</s>, and <s>Pārijātaka</s> are its names.
<s>Rohītaka</s> removes gulma, disorders of the liver and spleen, and abdominal disease.
<s>Mocaka</s> is <s>Mocarasa</s>; it is remembered as <s>Śālmalīveṣṭaka</s>.
It is <s>Mocaniryāsaka</s>, <s>Piccha</s>, <s>Mocasrāvī</s>, and <s>Veṣṭaka</s>.
<s>Mocaka</s> is cold, binding, heavy, aphrodisiac, and conquers diarrhea.
It removes pravāhikā, āma, vāta, blood disorders, phlegm, and burning.
<s>Ajagandhā</s> is <s>Bastagandhā</s>, <s>Kavarī</s>, and <s>Pūtibarbarī</s>.
<s>Ajagandhā</s> is light, appetizing, cardiac, and reduces blood disorders, phlegm, and vāta.
<s>Saireyaka</s> is <s>Sahacara</s>, <s>Saireya</s>, and <s>Kiṅkirātaka</s>.
It is <s>Dāsīsahacara</s>, <s>Jhiṇṭī</s>, <s>Sairyaka</s>, and <s>Mṛdukaṇṭaka</s>.
The red-flowered kind is <s>Kuravaka</s>; the yellow should be known as <s>Kuraṇṭaka</s>.
The blue is called <s>Ārtagala</s>, and also <s>Bāṇa</s> and <s>Odanapākī</s>.
<s>Saireya</s> removes skin disease, vāta, blood disorders, phlegm, itching, and poison.
It is bitter and hot, sweet, beneficial to the hair, very unctuous, and colors the hair.
<s>Śvetaspandā</s>, <s>Śvetapuṣpā</s>, <s>Kaṭabhī</s>, and <s>Girikarṇikā</s>,
<s>Sitāparājitā</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, <s>Viṣaghnī</s>, and <s>Mehanāśinī</s> are its names.
<s>Nīlaspandā</s>, <s>Vyaktagandhā</s>, <s>Nīlapuṣpā</s>, and <s>Gavādinī</s> are names of the blue kind.
The two kinds of <s>Śvetaspandā</s> are cold, remove graha disorders, and relieve eye itching.
They remove skin disease, colic, the three doṣas, āma, swelling, wounds, and poison.
<s>Ikṣura</s>, <s>Kṣuraka</s>, <s>Avyaṇḍa</s>, <s>Kokilākṣa</s>, and <s>Kṣura</s> are remembered.
<s>Tailakaṇṭa</s>, <s>Tikṣura</s>, <s>Ikṣuvālikā</s>, and <s>Ikṣugandhikā</s> are also names.
<s>Kṣuraka</s> is aphrodisiac, heavy, and conquers vāta, phlegm, and blood disorders.
<s>Kārpāsa</s> is <s>Paṭala</s>, <s>Tūla</s>, <s>Chādana</s>, <s>Bādara</s>, and <s>Picu</s>.
<s>Kārpāsaka</s> is light, mildly hot, sweet, and destroys vāta.
Its seed is aphrodisiac, unctuous, phlegm-producing, and heavy.
<s>Ārāmaśītalā</s>, <s>Devagandhā</s>, and <s>Kukkuramardana</s> are its names.
<s>Ārāmaśītalā</s> is cold and pungent, and conquers pitta, phlegm, and blood disorders.
<s>Kukkuradru</s> is <s>Tāmracūḍa</s>, with fine leaves and a soft covering.
<s>Kukkura</s> is pungent and bitter, and removes fever, blood disorders, and phlegm.

children.text: vāmī śaṅkhadharā dhārī brāhmī ca hilamocikā
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhadharā</s>, <s>Dhārī</s>, <s>Brāhmī</s>, and <s>Hilamocikā</s>,
are swelling-removing, and remove skin disease, pitta, and phlegm; it is flowing.
<s>Balā</s>, <s>Moṭā</s>, <s>Japā</s>, <s>Sūkṣmapattrā</s>, and <s>Aparājitā</s> should be known.
<s>Balā</s> removes poison, phlegm, and worms, and bestows victory.
<s>Śarapuṅkhā</s>, <s>Kālaśāka</s>, <s>Plīhāri</s>, and <s>Kālikā</s> are regarded as its names.
<s>Puṅkhā</s> removes disorders of the liver and spleen, bad wounds, and poison.
It is bitter, astringent, removes cough, dyspnea, and fever, and is light.
<s>Mayūrāhvā</s>, <s>Śikhā</s>, <s>Sāhasrī</s>, and <s>Madhukachadā</s> should be known.
<s>Mayūraśikhā</s> is light and conquers pitta, phlegm, and diarrhea.
<s>Lakṣmaṇā</s> is <s>Putradā</s>, <s>Raktabindupattrā</s>, and <s>Nāginī</s>.
Its flower resembles cow’s milk and is furnished with hair-like creepers.
A leaf marked with red spots is said to have the form of <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>.

children.text: lakṣmaṇā garbhadā śītā sarā vṛṣyā doṣanut ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s> promotes conception, is cold, flowing, aphrodisiac, and removes doṣas.
<s>Māṃsarohiṇī</s>, <s>Atiruhā</s>, <s>Vṛntā</s>, <s>Carmakaṣā</s>, and <s>Kasā</s>,
<s>Māṃsarohiṇī</s> is aphrodisiac, flowing, and removes the three doṣas.
<s>Asthisaṃhāraka</s> is <s>Vajravallarī</s> and <s>Kroṣṭughaṇṭikā</s>.
<s>Vajrāṅgī</s>, <s>Granthimān</s>, <s>Vajrī</s>, and <s>Asthiśṛṅkhalā</s> are declared as its names.
<s>Asthisaṃhāraka</s> is cold, aphrodisiac, vāta-removing, and beneficial for bones.
<s>Arka</s> is <s>Sūryāhvaya</s>, <s>Kṣīrī</s>, <s>Sadāpuṣpa</s>, and <s>Vikīraṇa</s>.
It is <s>Mandāra</s>, <s>Vasuka</s>, <s>Alarka</s>, <s>Rājārka</s>, and <s>Dīrghapuṣpaka</s>.
The two kinds of <s>Arka</s> are flowing and destroy vāta, skin disease, itching, graha disorders, and wounds.
They destroy splenic disease, gulma, piles, liver disease, colic, abdominal disease, and worms.
<s>Karavīra</s> is <s>Aśvahā</s>; the white-flowered kind is <s>Śvetakumbhaka</s>.
<s>Yāvānī</s>, <s>Yāvanī</s>, <s>Tīvrā</s>, <s>Turuṣkā</s>, and <s>Madakāriṇī</s>,

children.text: yavānī pācanī rūkṣā grāhiṇī mādinī guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yavānī</s> is digestive, dry, binding, intoxicating, and heavy.
<s>Khasatila</s> is a variety of sesame, white-flowered and with shining fruit.

children.text: vṛṣyo balyaḥ khasatilaḥ śleṣmalo vātajit guruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Khasatila</s> is aphrodisiac, strengthening, phlegmatic, vāta-conquering, and heavy.
The bark arising from its fruit is dry, binding, and desiccating.
<s>Aphūka</s>, produced from its sap, is <s>Ahiphena</s> and <s>Aphenaka</s>.
<s>Aphūka</s> is drying, binding, phlegm-destroying, and aggravates vāta and pitta.
<s>Chilihiṇṭa</s> is <s>Mahāmūla</s> and is called <s>Pātālagaruḍa</s>.
<s>Chilihiṇṭa</s> is supremely aphrodisiac, phlegmatic, and removes wind.

children.text: yo rājñāṃ mukhatilakaḥ kaṭāramalastena śrīmadananṛpeṇa nirmite'tra
children.translated_text: By that illustrious king <s>Madana</s>, who was the forehead ornament of kings and removed impurity like a dagger, in this work that he composed,
the section beginning with <s>Abhayā</s>, adorned with graceful words, has been completed in the book named <s>Madanavinoda</s>.
There, may the one supreme imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>-foot, beautiful with the lotus in its resplendent middle,

children.text: śrīmadanakṣitipāla sadā te viṣṇupadaṃ vipadaṃ vinihantu ||
children.translated_text: always destroy your calamity, O glorious king <s>Madanakṣitipāla</s>.

children.text: śuṇṭhī viśvauṣadhaṃ viśvaṃ kaṭu bhadraṃ kaṭūtkaṭam
children.translated_text: <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> is <s>Viśvauṣadha</s>, <s>Viśva</s>, pungent, auspicious, and intensely pungent.
It is <s>Mahauṣadha</s>, <s>Śṛṅgavera</s>, <s>Nāgara</s>, and <s>Viśvabheṣaja</s>.
<s>Śuṇṭhī</s> is appetizing, removes āma and vāta, is digestive, pungent, and light.
It is unctuous and hot, sweet in digestion, and removes obstruction caused by phlegm and vāta.
It is aphrodisiac and good for the voice, and it destroys vomiting, dyspnea, cough, colic, and heart disease.
It destroys elephantiasis, swelling, piles, abdominal distension, abdominal disease, and disorders of wind.
<s>Ārdraka</s> is <s>Śṛṅgavera</s>; it is declared to be a rhizome-medicine.
<s>Ārdraka</s> has the qualities of <s>Nāgara</s>; it is breaking, digestive-kindling, and heavy.
<s>Marica</s> is vine-born, sharp, dark-colored, black, and <s>Ūṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Marica</s> is pungent and sharp, stimulates digestion, and reduces kapha and vāta.
It is hot, produces pitta, is dry, and conquers dyspnea, cough, and worms.

children.text: tadārdraṃ madhuram pāke nātyuṣṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ guru
children.translated_text: When fresh, that is sweet in digestion, not excessively hot, pungent, and heavy.
It has a somewhat sharp quality, promotes salivation from phlegm, and is not pittala.

children.text: pippalī capalā kṛṣṇā māgadhī magadhā kaṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Pippalī</s> is <s>Capalā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Māgadhī</s>, <s>Magadhā</s>, and <s>Kaṇā</s>.
It is <s>Viśvopakulyā</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Śauṇḍī</s>, and <s>Tīkṣṇataṇḍulā</s>.
<s>Pippalī</s> kindles digestion, is aphrodisiac, sweet in digestion, and rejuvenative.
It is very hot, pungent, unctuous, removes kapha and vāta, and is light.
It is pittala and purgative, and destroys dyspnea, cough, abdominal disease, and fever.
It destroys skin disease, urinary disorders, abdominal tumors, piles, spleen disease, colic, undigested matter, and vāta.

children.text: ārdrā kaphapradā snigdhā śītalā madhurā guruḥ
children.translated_text: Fresh <s>Pippalī</s> produces kapha, is unctuous, cold, sweet, and heavy.
<s>Viśvopakulyā</s> together with <s>Marica</s> is the three <s>ūṣaṇa</s>; it is pungent and sharp.
It is <s>Vyoṣa</s> and the pungent triad; with <s>Granthi</s> it is the four <s>ūṣaṇa</s>.
The three <s>ūṣaṇa</s> stimulate digestion and destroy dyspnea, cough, and skin diseases.
They conquer abdominal tumors, urinary disorders, kapha, obesity, fat, filarial swelling, and nasal catarrh.
<s>Kaṇāmūla</s>, <s>Kaṭugranthi</s>, <s>Pippalīmūla</s>, and <s>Ūṣaṇa</s>,
<s>Ṣaḍgranthi</s>, <s>Granthika</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Magadha</s>, and <s>Caṭikāśiraḥ</s> are its names.
<s>Pippalīmūla</s> is digestive-kindling, pungent, hot, digestive, and light.
It is dry, produces pitta, is breaking, and removes kapha, vāta, and abdominal disease.
<s>Cavya</s> is called <s>Cavana</s>; it is <s>Cavikā</s> and <s>Kolavallikā</s>.
It is like <s>Pippalīmūla</s>, especially removing disorders born in the anus.
Its fruit is <s>Śreyasī</s>, <s>Hastimagadhī</s>, and <s>Gajapippalī</s>.
<s>Gajakṛṣṇā</s> is pungent, removes vāta and phlegm, and increases digestive fire.
It is hot and destroys diarrhea, dyspnea, throat diseases, and worms.
<s>Citraka</s> is <s>Hutabhuj</s>, <s>Vyāla</s>, <s>Dāruṇa</s>, <s>Dahana</s>, and <s>Aruṇa</s>.

children.text: dvīpī pālī haviḥ pāṭhī vahnināmā viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>Dvīpī</s>, <s>Pālī</s>, <s>Haviḥ</s>, <s>Pāṭhī</s>, and especially named after fire.
<s>Citraka</s> is pungent in digestion, cooks like fire, and is light.
It is dry and hot, and conquers grahaṇī disease, skin disease, swelling, piles, worms, and cough.
It removes phlegm and wind, is absorbent; its vegetable part conquers phlegm and pitta.
With <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Magadhāmūla</s>, <s>Cavya</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, and <s>Nāgara</s>,
the <s>Pañcakola</s> conquers kapha, abdominal distension, tumors, colic, and anorexia.
When joined with <s>Marica</s>, that is called the six <s>ūṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: śatapuṣpā śiphā śeṣā śatāhvā kāravī miśiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śatapuṣpā</s> is <s>Śiphā</s>, <s>Śeṣā</s>, <s>Śatāhvā</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, and <s>Miśi</s>.
It is <s>Avākpuṣpī</s>, <s>Tvaticchatrā</s>, <s>Śvetikā</s>, and another <s>Māgadhī</s>.
<s>Śatapuṣpā</s> is light and sharp, produces pitta, stimulates digestion, and is pungent.
It is hot and removes fever, wind, phlegm, wounds, colic, and eye disease.
<s>Śvetikā</s> is said to have the same qualities, but especially conquers uterine pain.
<s>Miśreyā</s>, <s>Miśi</s>, and <s>Śālinī</s> are considered <s>Śālī</s>, cold, and auspicious.
<s>Miśreyā</s> stimulates digestion, is heart-benefiting, and removes bound stool, worms, and skin disease.
Dry and hot, its fruit conquers cough, vomiting, phlegm, and wind.
<s>Methikā</s> is <s>Vastikā</s>, <s>Śelu</s>, <s>Ahilyā</s>, and <s>Vanamethikā</s>.

children.text: ahilyālpaguṇā tasmād vājināṃ sā tu pūjitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ahilyā</s> has slight qualities compared with that; but it is valued for horses.
<s>Ajamodā</s> is <s>Atyugragranthā</s>, <s>Modā</s>, <s>Hastimayūraka</s>,

children.text: kharāhvā kāravī vallī bastamodā ca markaṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kharāhvā</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, <s>Vallī</s>, <s>Bastamodā</s>, and <s>Markaṭa</s>.
<s>Ajamodā</s> is pungent, sharp, digestive-kindling, and removes kapha and vāta.

children.text: uṣṇā vidāhinī hṛdyā vṛṣyā baddhamalā laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is hot, burning, heart-benefiting, aphrodisiac, constipating, and light.
It conquers eye disease, worms, vomiting, sidhma skin disease, and bladder pain.
<s>Jīraka</s> is <s>Dīrghaka</s>, <s>Śukla</s>, <s>Ajājī</s>, and <s>Kaṇajīraka</s>.
<s>Jīraka</s> is <s>Jaraṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and fragrant in the rainy season.
<s>Kalikā</s>, <s>Bāṣpikā</s>, <s>Kuñci</s>, and <s>Kāravī</s> are also <s>Upakuñcikā</s>.
<s>Pṛthvīkā</s>, <s>Suṣavī</s>, <s>Pṛthvī</s>, <s>Sthūlājājī</s>, and <s>Upakālikā</s> are names.
The three kinds of <s>Jīraka</s> are dry, pungent, hot, digestive-kindling, and light.
They are absorbent, pittala, intellect-promoting, and purify the womb.
They benefit the eyes and conquer wind, abdominal distension, tumors, vomiting, and balāsa.
<s>Yavānī</s> is <s>Dīpyaka</s>, <s>Dīpya</s>, <s>Dīpanīyā</s>, and <s>Yavānikā</s>.
It is <s>Yavasāhā</s>, <s>Ugragandhā</s>, <s>Yavāhvā</s>, and <s>Bhūkadambaka</s>.

children.text: yavānī pācanī rucyā tīkṣṇoṣṇā kaṭukā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yavānī</s> is digestive, appetizing, sharp, hot, pungent, and light.
It conquers vāta, phlegm, abdominal disease, distension, colic, and worms.
<s>Yavānīyā</s> is a kind of <s>Yavānī</s>; <s>Cauhāra</s> destroys living creatures.
<s>Cauhāra</s> is said to have its qualities, but especially destroys worms.
<s>Ajagandhā</s> is <s>Pūtikīṭā</s>, <s>Barbarī</s>, and <s>Pūtibarbara</s>.
It is <s>Kāravī</s>, <s>Kharapuṣpā</s>, <s>Tuṅgī</s>, and <s>Pūtimayūraka</s>.
<s>Ajagandhā</s> is pungent, sharp, dry, heart-benefiting, and increases digestive fire.
It causes dullness of sight, is light, and removes semen disorders, vāta, and kapha.
<s>Vacā</s> is <s>Ugragandhā</s>, <s>Golomī</s>, <s>Ṣaḍgranthā</s>, and is considered <s>Jaṭilā</s>.
<s>Jaṭilā</s> is another <s>Śataparvā</s>; it is also <s>Lomaśā</s> and <s>Hemavatī</s>.
<s>Vacā</s> is hot, pungent, bitter, emetic, and produces voice and digestive fire.
It conquers epilepsy, phlegm, insanity, possession, colic, and wind.
<s>Hapuṣā</s> is <s>Vapuṣā</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, <s>Vigandhā</s>, and <s>Viśvagandhikā</s>.

children.text: hapuṣā dīpanī tiktā kaṭūṣṇā tuvarā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hapuṣā</s> stimulates digestion, is bitter, pungent, hot, astringent, and heavy.
It conquers pitta, abdominal disease, wind, piles, grahaṇī disease, swelling, and tumors.
<s>Viḍaṅga</s> is <s>Jantuhanana</s>, <s>Kṛmighna</s>, and <s>Kṣudrataṇḍulā</s>.
It is <s>Bhūtaghnī</s>, <s>Taṇḍulā</s>, <s>Ghoṣā</s>, <s>Karālā</s>, and <s>Mṛgagāminī</s>.

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ kaṭu tiktoṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ vahnikaraṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍaṅga</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, dry, digestive-fire-producing, and light.
It removes tumors, distension, abdominal disease, phlegm, worms, vāta, and constipation.

children.text: dhānyākaṃ dhānyakaṃ dhānyaṃ dhāneyaṃ ca vitunnakam
children.translated_text: <s>Dhānyāka</s> is <s>Dhānyaka</s>, <s>Dhānya</s>, <s>Dhāneya</s>, and <s>Vitunnaka</s>.
<s>Kustumburu</s>, when fresh, is <s>Dhānī</s>, <s>Dhāneyaka</s>, and <s>Ālukā</s>.
<s>Dhānyaka</s> is astringent, oily, non-aphrodisiac, diuretic, and light.

children.text: hṛdyaṃ rūkṣaṃ baddhaviṭkaṃ svādu pāke tridoṣanut ||
children.translated_text: It benefits the heart, is dry, constipating, sweet in digestion, and removes the three doṣas.
It is digestive and conquers dyspnea, cough, blood disorders, thirst, piles, and worms.
<s>Āhnīkā</s> has those same qualities; it is sweet and especially destroys pitta.
<s>Hiṅgupattrī</s>, <s>Pṛthustanvī</s>, <s>Pṛthvīkā</s>, and <s>Cārupattrikā</s>,

children.text: bāṣpikā kāravī tanvī bilvikā dīrghikā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bāṣpikā</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, <s>Tanvī</s>, <s>Bilvikā</s>, and likewise <s>Dīrghikā</s>,
<s>Hiṅgupattrī</s>, the superior one, <s>Veṇupattrī</s>, and <s>Hiṅguśivāṭikā</s>,

children.text: jantukā rāmaṭhī nāḍī piṇḍā hiṅguphalā matā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jantukā</s>, <s>Rāmaṭhī</s>, <s>Nāḍī</s>, and <s>Piṇḍā</s> are considered names of <s>Hiṅguphalā</s>.
The two kinds of <s>Hiṅgupattrī</s> benefit the heart, are sharp, hot, digestive, and pungent.
They remove pain in the heart and bladder, constipation, piles, phlegm, gulma, and wind.
<s>Hiṅgu</s> is <s>Bāhlīka</s>, extremely fierce, <s>Rāmaṭha</s>, and <s>Bhūtanāśana</s>.
It is <s>Agūḍhagandha</s>, digestive, <s>Jantuka</s>, and destroyer of colic.
<s>Hiṅgu</s> is hot, digestive, appetizing, sharp, hot, and conquers kapha and vāta.
It conquers colic, gulma, abdominal disease, distension, and worms, and increases pitta.
<s>Vaṃśajā</s>, <s>Vaiṇavī</s>, <s>Kṣīrī</s>, <s>Tvakkṣīrī</s>, and <s>Vaṃśarocanā</s>,

children.text: tugākṣīrī tugā vāṃśī vaṃśakṣīrī śubhā sitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tugākṣīrī</s>, <s>Tugā</s>, <s>Vāṃśī</s>, <s>Vaṃśakṣīrī</s>, auspicious, and white,

children.text: bṛṃhaṇī vaṃśajā vṛṣyā śītalā madhurā jayet
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṃśajā</s> is nourishing, aphrodisiac, cooling, and sweet; it conquers
thirst, fever, wasting, dyspnea, cough, pitta, blood disorders, and jaundice.
<s>Saindhava</s>, born from the Sindhu, pure, <s>Māṇimantha</s>, and the best of salts,

children.text: saindhavaṃ madhuraṃ hṛdyaṃ dīpanaṃ śītalaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> is sweet, heart-benefiting, digestive-kindling, cooling, and light.
It benefits the eyes, is digestive, oily, aphrodisiac, and removes the three doṣas.
<s>Sauvarcala</s> is <s>Sugandhākṣa</s>, <s>Rucaka</s>, and <s>Pūtigandhaka</s>.
<s>Sauvarcala</s> produces digestive fire, is pungent, hot, clear, and light.
It purifies belching, is subtle, and conquers constipation, abdominal distension, and colic.

children.text: viḍaṃ kṛtrimakam pākyaṃ dhūrtaṃ drāviḍam āsuram
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍa</s> is <s>Kṛtrimaka</s>, <s>Pākya</s>, <s>Dhūrta</s>, <s>Drāviḍa</s>, and <s>Āsura</s>.
<s>Viḍa</s> is light and hot, and destroys obstruction, colic, cardiac heaviness, and anorexia.
It destroys distension and kapha, is subtle, and guides downward-moving wind in its proper course.
<s>Sāmudra</s> is sea-born, water-born, <s>Akṣīva</s>, and also <s>Vaśira</s>.

children.text: sāmudraṃ dīpanaṃ svādu nātyuṣṇam bhedanaṃ kaṭu
children.translated_text: <s>Sāmudra</s> kindles digestion, is sweet, not excessively hot, purgative, and pungent.
It increases phlegm, removes wind, is bitter, not dry, and not very pittala.
<s>Audbhida</s> is earth-born, terrestrial, earthly, and produced from the earth.
<s>Audbhida</s> promotes blood, is subtle and light, and directs vāta downward.
The salt called <s>Gaḍa</s> is <s>Romalavaṇa</s>, <s>Roma</s>, and produced in <s>Śākambharī</s>.

children.text: gaḍākhyaṃ laghu vātaghnam atyuṣṇam bhedi mūtralam ||
children.translated_text: The one called <s>Gaḍa</s> is light, removes vāta, is very hot, purgative, and diuretic.
<s>Kṣāra</s> is earth-born, <s>Tauṣama</s>, saline-soil-born, dust-born, and <s>Vasu</s>.

children.text: kṣāraṃ guru kaṭu snigdhaṃ śleṣmalaṃ vātanāśanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣāra</s> is heavy, pungent, oily, phlegm-producing, and destroys vāta.
<s>Kāca</s> is <s>Trikūṭa</s>, called <s>Pākya</s>, a salt, and produced from glass.
<s>Kāca</s> kindles digestion, is very hot, and greatly increases blood and pitta.
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> is cooked from barley-awn, <s>Yāvaśūka</s>, and elder-born of barley.
<s>Svarjikā</s> is <s>Svarjikāpākya</s>, <s>Sukhavarcas</s>, and <s>Suvarci</s>.
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> produces digestive fire and conquers vāta, phlegm, dyspnea, and throat diseases.
It conquers āma, piles, grahaṇī disease, gulma, and pains of the liver and spleen.
<s>Svarjikā</s> has lesser qualities than that, but especially conquers gulma and colic.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is born from <s>Mālatī</s>, is dissolving, and purifies iron.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> produces digestive fire, is dry, destroys kapha, and produces vāta and pitta.
<s>Sudhā</s>, called <s>Amṛta</s>, is <s>Saudhabhūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Kaṭhaśarkarā</s>.
<s>Sudhākṣāra</s> is like fire, ripening, moistening, and splitting open.
Those born from palāśa, sesame stalk, horse's-tooth, and banana,
and those arising from <s>Apāmārga</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Sehuṇḍa</s>, <s>Muṣkaka</s>, and the like,
all alkalis are like fire, digestive, purgative, and splitting.
They are light, cutting, sharp, and destructive of semen, ojas, and eyesight.
They produce blood and pitta, and destroy constipation, abdominal distension, and chronic rhinitis,
as well as disorders of the liver and spleen, balāsa, āma, gulma, piles, grahaṇī disease, and worms.

children.text: yo rājñām pūrṇaḥ śuṇṭhyādiḥ khalu bhiṣajāṃ hitāya vargaḥ
children.translated_text: This group beginning with <s>Śuṇṭhī</s>, full for kings, is indeed for the benefit of physicians.
Thus, in the nighaṇṭu composed by the illustrious <s>Madanapāla</s>, the second group, beginning with <s>Śuṇṭhī</s>, is complete.

children.text: yadvāñchayā viśvakṛto'pi devā brahmādayo yānti muhurbhavanti
children.translated_text: Desiring whom, even the gods, makers of the universe, such as <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, again and again come into being,

children.text: acintyakṛtyaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ gopatvam āptaṃ tamupāśrayāmi ||
children.translated_text: I take refuge in that inconceivably acting, primeval person who has attained the state of cowherd.
<s>Suvarṇa</s>, <s>Kāñcana</s>, <s>Hema</s>, <s>Hāṭaka</s>, and <s>Taptakāñcana</s>,
<s>Cāmīkara</s>, <s>Śātakumbha</s>, <s>Tapanīya</s>, and also <s>Rukmaka</s>,
<s>Jāmbūnada</s>, <s>Hiraṇya</s>, <s>Svarala</s>, and <s>Jātarūpaka</s> are names of gold.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ śītalaṃ vṛṣyaṃ balyaṃ guru rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇa</s> is cooling, aphrodisiac, strengthening, heavy, and a rasāyana.
It gives luster and conquers poison, insanity, the three doṣas, fever, and wasting.
<s>Suvarṇa</s> is astringent, bitter-sweet, heavy, and scraping.

children.text: rūpyakaṃ rajataṃ rūpyaṃ tāraṃ śvetaṃ vasūttamam
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpyaka</s>, <s>Rajata</s>, <s>Rūpya</s>, <s>Tāra</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and excellent <s>Vasu</s> are names of silver.
<s>Rūpya</s> is cooling, flowing, removes vāta and pitta, and is a rasāyana.

children.text: lekhanaṃ ca kaṣāyāmlaṃ vipāke cāparaṃ saram
children.translated_text: It is also scraping, astringent-sour, and, in post-digestive effect, otherwise flowing.
It preserves age, is oily, and is said to be beneficial to the bodily elements.
<s>Tāmra</s> is <s>Mlecchamukha</s>, <s>Śulva</s>, <s>Naipāla</s>, and called <s>Ravi</s>.
It is <s>Udumbara</s>, <s>Sūryapriya</s>, <s>Raktaja</s>, and <s>Raktadhātuka</s>.

children.text: tāmraṃ saraṃ laghu svādu śītaṃ pittakaphāpaham
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmra</s> is flowing, light, sweet, cooling, and removes pitta and kapha.
It heals and conquers anemia, skin disease, piles, swelling, dyspnea, and cough.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ lohaṃ nijaṃ ghoṣaṃ pañcalohaṃ prakāśakam
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṃsya</s> is <s>Loha</s>, <s>Nija</s>, <s>Ghoṣa</s>, <s>Pañcaloha</s>, and <s>Prakāśaka</s>.
<s>Kāṃsya</s> is heavy, hot, beneficial for the eyes, removes kapha and pitta, and is flowing.
<s>Pītaloha</s>, <s>Siṃhalaka</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and <s>Saukumāraka</s>,
<s>Vartaloha</s>, <s>Triloha</s>, <s>Rājarīti</s>, and <s>Maheśvarī</s> are names of brass.
<s>Pītaloha</s> is cooling, dry, pungent, hot, and removes kapha and pitta.

children.text: raṅkakaṃ tīrakaṃ vaṅgaṃ trapu syātkaraṭī ghanam
children.translated_text: <s>Raṅkaka</s>, <s>Tīraka</s>, <s>Vaṅga</s>, and <s>Trapu</s> are names; it is also <s>Karaṭī</s> and <s>Ghana</s>.
<s>Raṅga</s> is light, flowing, dry, and hot; it destroys urinary disease, kapha, and worms.
It destroys pāṇḍu disease together with asthma, is beneficial to sight, and is slightly pittala.
<s>Jasada</s> is similar to <s>Raṅka</s>; it is regarded as the cause of shining whiteness.
<s>Jasada</s> is astringent, bitter, cooling, and removes kapha and pitta.

children.text: cakṣuṣyaṃ paramaṃ mehān pāṇḍuṃ śvāsaṃ ca nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: It is supremely good for the eyes and destroys urinary diseases, pāṇḍu disease, and asthma.
<s>Sīsa</s>, <s>Dhātumala</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Uraga</s>, and <s>Paripiṣṭaka</s> are names.

children.text: javaneṣṭaṃ ca bhujagaṃ visṛṣṭaṃ kṛṣṇakaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: It is known as <s>Javaneṣṭa</s>, <s>Bhujaga</s>, <s>Visṛṣṭa</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇaka</s>.
<s>Sīsa</s> should be understood to have the qualities of <s>Raṅga</s>, and especially to destroy urinary disease.

children.text: lohaṃ śastram ayaḥ kuṣṭhaṃ vyaṅgaṃ pārāvataṃ ghanam
children.translated_text: <s>Loha</s>, <s>Śastra</s>, <s>Ayaḥ</s>, <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>Vyaṅga</s>, <s>Pārāvata</s>, and <s>Ghana</s> are names.
Its refuse is <s>Kṛṣṇāyas</s>; the slag is <s>Kiṭṭa</s>, <s>Maṇḍūra</s>, and dust born from iron.

children.text: lohaṃ saraṃ guru svādu kaṣāyaṃ kaphapittanut
children.translated_text: <s>Loha</s> is flowing, heavy, sweet, astringent, and removes kapha and pitta.

children.text: śītaṃ netrahitaṃ rūkṣaṃ balyaṃ vātalam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: It is cooling, beneficial to the eyes, dry, strengthening, vāta-producing, and excellent.
It conquers swelling, skin disease, urinary disease, piles, poison, pāṇḍu disease, and worms.
Its slag should be understood to have the same qualities, and especially to destroy pāṇḍu disease.
<s>Pārada</s> is <s>Capala</s>, <s>Hemanidhi</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, and <s>Rasottama</s>.

children.text: trinetro roṣaṇaḥ svāmī harabījaṃ rasaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>Trinetra</s>, <s>Roṣaṇa</s>, <s>Svāmī</s>, <s>Harabīja</s>, <s>Rasa</s>, and <s>Prabhu</s>.
It is famous as <s>Rasendra</s>, and is <s>Rasaloha</s> and <s>Mahārasa</s>.
<s>Pārada</s> destroys worms and skin disease, is beneficial to the eyes, hot, and rejuvenating.
<s>Abhraka</s> is <s>Svaccha</s>, <s>Ākāśa</s>, <s>Paṭala</s>, and <s>Varapītaka</s>.
<s>Abhra</s> is heavy, cooling, strengthening, and removes skin disease, urinary disease, and the three doṣas.

children.text: gaganaṃ kṛmikuṣṭhamehahṛd viśadaṃ śukrakaraṃ ca dīpanam
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana</s> removes worms, skin disease, and urinary disease; it is clear, semen-producing, and digestive-kindling.

children.text: kathitaṃ munibhiśca pūrvajair balyakṛcchukrakaraṃ ca sevitam ||
children.translated_text: The ancient sages have said that, when used, it produces strength and semen.
<s>Gandhaka</s> is <s>Saugandhaka</s>, <s>Lekhī</s>, <s>Gandhāśman</s>, and <s>Gandhapītaka</s>.
It is <s>Lelītaka</s>, <s>Balivasā</s>, <s>Vegandha</s>, <s>Gandhaka</s>, and <s>Bali</s>.

children.text: gandhakaḥ kaṭukaḥ pāke vīryoṣṇaḥ pittalaḥ saraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhaka</s> is pungent in digestion, hot in potency, pittala, and flowing.
It destroys skin disease, wasting, spleen disease, kapha, vāta, and disorders of rasa.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, <s>Dhātumākṣīka</s>, <s>Tāpya</s>, and <s>Tāpīja</s> are names.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tuvaraṃ vṛṣyaṃ svaryaṃ laghu rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is astringent, aphrodisiac, good for the voice, light, and rejuvenating.
It is beneficial to the eyes and removes skin disease, swelling, piles, urinary disease, bladder pain, and pāṇḍu disease.
It is diffusive and pungent, and destroys skin disease, abdominal disease, poison, and wasting.

children.text: manaḥśilā śilā golā naipālī kunaṭī kulā
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s> is <s>Śilā</s>, <s>Golā</s>, <s>Naipālī</s>, <s>Kunaṭī</s>, and <s>Kulā</s>.
It is <s>Divyauṣadhi</s>, <s>Nāgamātā</s>, <s>Manoguptā</s>, and <s>Mano'mbikā</s>.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> removes dysuria, is flowing, hot, scraping, and pungent.
It is bitter and unctuous, and conquers poison, asthma, cough, spirits, kapha, and blood disorders.
<s>Haritāla</s> is <s>Mala</s>, <s>Tāla</s>, <s>Godanta</s>, and <s>Naṭabhūṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: haritālaṃ kaṭu snigdhaṃ kaṣāyoṣṇaṃ viṣaṃ jayet
children.translated_text: <s>Haritāla</s> is pungent, unctuous, astringent, and hot; it conquers poison.
It also conquers itching, skin disease, mouth diseases, kapha, pitta, and disorders of the hair.
<s>Gairika</s> is <s>Raktapāṣāṇa</s>, <s>Girimṛd</s>, and <s>Gavedhuka</s>.
<s>Svarṇavarṇa</s>, <s>Para</s>, <s>Svarṇamaṇḍala</s>, and <s>Svarṇagairika</s> are names.
<s>Gairika</s> removes burning, pitta, blood disorders, kapha, hiccup, and poison.
Another kind is similarly beneficial to the eyes, and especially destroys vomiting.
<s>Tuttha</s>, <s>Karpūrikātuttha</s>, and <s>Amṛtāsaṅga</s> are names.
Another is <s>Mayūragrīvaka</s>, and <s>Śikhikaṇṭha</s> is also <s>Tutthaka</s>.
<s>Tutthaka</s> is scraping and purgative, and removes itching, skin disease, and poison.
It likewise removes kapha and worms, and another kind is excellent for the eyes.
<s>Kāsīsa</s>, <s>Dhātukāsīsa</s>, <s>Khecara</s>, and <s>Taptalomaśa</s> are names.
Another, <s>Puṣpakāsīsa</s>, is astringent and gives color to cloth.
The two kinds of <s>Kāsīsa</s> are sour, hot, bitter, good for the hair, and beneficial to sight.
They destroy itching, poison, white leprosy, dysuria, kapha, and vāta.
<s>Hiṅgula</s>, <s>Darada</s>, <s>Mleccha</s>, <s>Saikata</s>, and <s>Cūrṇapārada</s> are names.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> removes pitta and kapha, is beneficial to the eyes, and removes poison and skin disease.
<s>Sindūra</s> is <s>Nāgaja</s>, <s>Rakta</s>, and the splendid ornament of adornment.
It is <s>Vasantamaṇḍana</s>, <s>Nāgarakta</s>, and also <s>Raktarajas</s>.
<s>Sindūra</s> is hot and removes erysipelas, skin disease, itching, and poison.
It generates the joining of fractures, and cleanses and heals wounds.
<s>Sauvīramañjana</s> is black, dark-blue, and born in <s>Suvīra</s>.

children.text: srotoñjanaṃ tu srotojaṃ nadījaṃ yāmunaṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Srotoñjana</s> is <s>Srotoja</s>, river-born, and the best is from the <s>Yamunā</s>.
<s>Sauvīra</s> is absorbent, sweet, beneficial to the eyes, and conquers kapha and vāta.
It removes sidhma skin disease, wasting, and blood disorders; <s>Sroto'ñjana</s> is similar and cooling.

children.text: rasāñjanaṃ rasodbhūtaṃ tārkṣyaṃ śailaṃ ca tārkṣyajam
children.translated_text: <s>Rasāñjana</s> is produced from rasa; it is <s>Tārkṣya</s>, <s>Śaila</s>, and <s>Tārkṣyaja</s>.
<s>Rasāgrya</s>, the artificial <s>Tārkṣya</s>, is <s>Dārvya</s>, produced from the juice of <s>Dārvī</s>.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is pungent and conquers disorders of phlegm, the mouth, and the eyes.
It is hot, rejuvenating, bitter, cutting, and conquers faults of wounds.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s>, <s>Puṣpaketu</s>, <s>Rītija</s>, and <s>Kusumāñjana</s> are names.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is alkaline and hot, and removes cataract and film over the eye.
<s>Śilājatu</s>, born from heat, is the exudation of mountains and is called <s>Giriśa</s>.
<s>Śilāhva</s>, <s>Girija</s>, <s>Śaila</s>, <s>Śaileya</s>, and <s>Girija</s> are also names.
<s>Śilājatu</s> is hot, pungent, a carrier in compound preparations, and rejuvenating.
It destroys vomiting, urinary disease, vāta disorders, piles, skin disease, mouth disease, abdominal disease, and pāṇḍu disease.
It also destroys asthma, wasting, insanity, blood disorders, swelling, kapha, and worms.

children.text: bolaṃ gandharasaṃ vīraṃ nirlohaṃ barbaraṃ calam
children.translated_text: <s>Bola</s>, <s>Gandharasa</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, <s>Nirloha</s>, <s>Barbara</s>, and <s>Cala</s> are names.

children.text: sugandhi nālikā piṇḍaṃ rasagandhaṃ ca taddvidhā ||
children.translated_text: It is fragrant; <s>Nālikā</s>, <s>Piṇḍa</s>, and <s>Rasagandha</s> are its two forms.
<s>Bola</s> removes blood disorders, is cooling, intellect-promoting, digestive-kindling, and digestive.
It destroys fever, epilepsy, and skin disease, and purifies the womb.
<s>Sphaṭikākhyā</s> is <s>Mṛtā</s>, <s>Bāṣpī</s>, <s>Kakṣī</s>, and that which arises in <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>.
<s>Āḍakī</s>, <s>Tuvarā</s>, another <s>Mṛttikā</s>, and <s>Suramṛttikā</s> are its names.
<s>Sphaṭikākhyā</s> is astringent and hot, and destroys kapha, pitta, poison, and wounds.
It also destroys white leprosy and erysipelas; <s>Tuvarī</s> is considered to have the same qualities.
<s>Samudraphena</s> is <s>Ḍiṇḍīra</s>, <s>Phena</s>, <s>Vārikapha</s>, and <s>Dvija</s>.
<s>Samudraphena</s> benefits the eyes, is scraping, pacifying, and laxative.
<s>Pravāla</s> is <s>Vidruma</s>, <s>Sindhura</s>, <s>Latāgra</s>, and red in color.
It gives nourishment and beauty, is strengthening, and increases strength and semen.

children.text: mauktikaṃ tautilā muktāphalaṃ muktā ca śuktijam
children.translated_text: <s>Mauktika</s> is <s>Tautilā</s>, <s>Muktāphala</s>, <s>Muktā</s>, and shell-born.
<s>Mauktika</s> is sweet and cold, destroys diseases, and destroys poison.
<s>Māṇikya</s> is <s>Padmarāga</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Ratna</s>, and <s>Suratnaka</s>.
<s>Sūryakānta</s> is <s>Sūryamaṇi</s>, <s>Sūryākṣa</s>, and <s>Dahanopala</s>.
<s>Candrakānta</s> is <s>Candramaṇi</s>, <s>Sphaṭika</s>, and <s>Sphaṭikopala</s>.

children.text: gomedaṃ sundaraṃ pītaṃ ratnaṃ tṛṇacaraṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gomeda</s> is beautiful, yellow, a jewel, and also <s>Tṛṇacara</s>.
<s>Hīraka</s> is <s>Bhidura</s>, <s>Vajra</s>, <s>Sūcīvaktra</s>, and <s>Varāhaka</s>.
<s>Nīlaratna</s> is <s>Nīlamaṇi</s>, <s>Vaiḍūrya</s>, and <s>Bālavāyaja</s>.
<s>Gārutmata</s> is <s>Marakata</s>, <s>Dṛṣadgarbha</s>, and <s>Harinmaṇi</s>.
<s>Muktāsphoṭa</s> is <s>Abdhimaṇḍūkī</s>, <s>Śukti</s>, and the abode of pearls.
Coral, pearl, ruby, sun-stone, and moon-stone,
together with gomeda, diamond, vaiḍūrya, sapphire, gārutmata, and the rest,

children.text: cakṣuṣyā lekhanāḥ śītāḥ kaṣāyā madhurāḥ sarāḥ
children.translated_text: benefit the eyes, are scraping, cold, astringent, sweet, and laxative.
They are auspicious; when worn, they remove burning, evil spirits, and poison.
<s>Śaṅkha</s> is <s>Kambu</s>, <s>Jaladhara</s>, <s>Vārija</s>, and long-sounding.

children.text: śaṅkho hi kaṭukaḥ pāke kaṣāyo madhuro laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkha</s>, indeed, is pungent in digestion, astringent, sweet, and light.
It benefits the eyes, is scraping, and destroys digestive colic and pitta.
<s>Śaṅkha</s> is good for the eyes, cold, light, and conquers pitta, kapha, and blood disorders.
<s>Śaṅkha</s>, the small conch, <s>Śambuka</s>, and water-shells
are to be known as <s>Kaparda</s>, <s>Kṣullaka</s>, <s>Varāṭa</s>, and <s>Varāṭikā</s>.
The small conch and related substances are cold and destroy eye-pain and eruptions.
<s>Khaṭī</s>, <s>Makkolla</s>, <s>Khaṭinī</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, and <s>Nāḍītaraṅgaka</s> are names.
Its variety is called <s>Gauḍapāṣāṇa</s> and <s>Kṣīrapāka</s>.
<s>Khaṭī</s> removes burning and blood disorders and is cold; <s>Gauḍagrāva</s> too has those qualities.

children.text: paṅkaḥ kardamako jñeyo vālukā sikatā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Paṅka</s> is known as <s>Kardamaka</s>; <s>Vālukā</s> is also <s>Sikatā</s>.
<s>Paṅka</s> destroys burning, blood disorders, pitta-pain, and swelling; it is cooling and laxative.
<s>Vālukā</s> is scraping and cold, and destroys wounds and chest injuries.
<s>Cumbaka</s> is <s>Kāntapāṣāṇa</s>, <s>Ayaskānta</s>, and drawer of iron.
<s>Cumbaka</s> is scraping and cold, and removes fat, poison, and artificial poison.
<s>Kāca</s> is artificial jewel; <s>Piṅgāṇa</s> is a glass vessel.
<s>Kāca</s> is splitting, suitable for wounds, beneficial to the eyes, scraping, and light.

children.text: yo rājñāṃ mukhatilakaḥ kaṭāramallas tena śrīmadananṛpeṇa nirmite'tra
children.translated_text: By that illustrious king <s>Madana</s>, who was the forehead-mark of kings and a champion in battle, this
variegated <s>Suvarṇavarga</s>, full of elegant words, was completed in the book named <s>Madanavinoda</s>, composed by him.
